title: Book of Jubilees — Restored Names Edition
front_matter:
Title Page

The Book of Jubilees

Restored Names Edition

With Verse-by-Verse Commentary

Yoshi Remnant of Promise

Introduction

The Book of Jubilees is not new. The book is older than the New
Testament. It was read in Yashar’el (Israel) before the Messiah (Christ)
walked the dust of Galilee. It was preserved at Qumran among the sect
that watched for him. It was carried into Ethiopia by the body that
received it as scripture and kept it in its canon when no one else
would. The early assemblies in the West read it — Jude alludes to it,
the framework of his own short letter is unintelligible without the
Watchers material it shares with 1 Enoch and Jubilees — and then, at the
same Council of Laodicea (363 AD) where the horn moved the Sabbath and
pulled 1 Enoch out of the canon, Jubilees was set aside too. Not because
it was wrong. Because it said too clearly what the body the horn was
building had decided not to say.

What does Jubilees say, that the four houses needed silenced?

It says the Sabbath is older than Sinai. It says the Sabbath was kept in
heaven before any flesh kept it on the earth. It says the angels of the
presence and the angels of sanctification keep the Sabbath with Yahuah
(God) — and that he hallowed a peculiar people above all peoples to keep
it together with them. It says the seventh day is the rest of the
Creator, sealed at creation, ratified into the calendar of heaven, given
to the covenant body as a sign for ever. The day cannot be moved. The
horn moved it.

It says the festivals — the Feast of Weeks, the Feast of Tabernacles,
the Passover — are not Yahudi (Jewish) holidays Christianity has
graduated from. They are appointed times engraven on the heavenly tables
before Sinai. The Feast of Weeks was kept in heaven from creation, kept
on earth by Noah, kept by Abraham, kept by Isaac, kept by Jacob,
re-disclosed at Sinai to a body that had forgotten it in Egypt, kept by
the Messiah (Christ) himself, and folded into the architecture of the
gathering at the end of the age. The festivals were not retired. The
body forgot.

It says the festivals are appointed times engraven on the heavenly
tables, marked by the two lights Genesis 1:14 set together for signs and
seasons — the moon’s own witness naming the new month as Psalm 81 has
it, the seventh-day rhythm Yahuah (God) hallowed at creation. Where the
book of Jubilees presses further than this — setting the moon aside and
locking the year against its witness — the commentary on chapters 2 and
6 presses back.

It says the Watchers descended in the days of Jared, took wives of the
daughters of men, taught the omens of the sun and moon and stars and the
metallurgy of war, fathered the giants, and corrupted the orders of
every flesh on the earth. It says their offspring drowned in the Flood —
but their disembodied spirits are the unclean demons that walk the earth
from then on, and the chief of those spirits is Mastema, the prince of
accusations, whom Yahuah (God) permitted to retain a tenth of the bound
spirits at his command until the appointed end. This architecture is not
the church’s architecture. The church flattened the Watchers into the
godly line of Seth and the daughters of men into the wicked line of Cain
— a fourth-century invention the church needed because it had withdrawn
1 Enoch and Jubilees from the canon and could not afford to keep the
original reading. Peter and Jude both refuse the flattening (2 Peter
2:4; Jude 6). Jubilees gives the architecture in full.

It says the holy line descends from Adam through Seth, Enoch,
Methuselah, Lamech, Noah, Shem, Eber, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob — and
that Adam was a priest before there was a priesthood, that the priestly
office is older than Levi, that the tithe is older than Aaron, that the
festivals are older than the wilderness wanderings the festivals will
later commemorate. All of Sinai, in Jubilees’ frame, is the
re-disclosure to a covenant body in Egypt of what the body’s fathers had
already carried. Sinai is not novelty. Sinai is recovery.

It says the seed of Jacob — the twelve tribes through their patriarch —
is the firstborn son of Yahuah (God). The firstborn-son language
Jubilees uses in chapter 2:20 is the same language Yahuah (God) will
speak to Pharaoh in Exodus 4:22, and the same language the prophets will
speak again of the gathered house. The covenant body is real. The
covenant body is named. The covenant body has a paternal blood lineage
that the prophets traced and promised to gather. Christianity says the
church replaced this body. Judaism says only Yahudah (Judah) carries it.
Hebrew roots says anyone who keeps Torah replaces it. Islam says the
covenant transferred to Ishmael. Four houses. Four denials. Four
versions of the same lie.

Jubilees forecloses every one of them. Chapter 15:30–31 is the verse the
four houses cannot hold: over Yashar’el (Israel) He did not appoint any
angel or spirit, for He alone is their ruler. The covenant people are
the seed of Jacob, under the direct rule of Yahuah (God), distinct from
the nations who were placed under intermediate authorities, distinct
from Ishmael’s line and Esau’s line who are blessed in their own measure
but are not the seed of promise. The chapter is unbothered by modern
sensibilities. It states the architecture and lets the architecture
speak.

And it says — this is the verse the awakening reader must let land — the
body that forgot will be gathered. Chapter 1:15 onward names what every
prophet later confirms: they will turn to Me from amongst the nations
with all their heart and with all their soul and with all their
strength, and I shall gather them from amongst all the nations. The
gathering is not metaphor. The gathering is not the church. The
gathering is the paternal blood remnant of all twelve tribes of
Yashar’el (Israel) coming home — Yahudah (Judah) and the scattered house
of the north, Ephraim and Yosef and Yashar’el (Israel), the lost sheep
that Yahusha (Jesus) said he was sent to (Matthew 15:24), the Lo-Ammi of
Hosea 1 to whom the second word came in the same chapter: in the place
where it was said unto them, ye are not my people, there it shall be
said unto them, ye are the sons of the living Elohim (God). Paul quotes
that verse in Romans 9:25–26. He knew who he was writing to. The
scattered seed is being gathered, and this is the second recovery the
prophets named.

Chapter 23:26 is the verse the awakening reader will not be able to put
down: in those days the children will begin to study the laws, and to
seek the commandments, and to return to the path of righteousness. Read
it slowly. The recovery does not start in the synagogues of the
surviving Yahudim (Jews). The recovery does not start in the academies
of institutional Christianity. The recovery starts in the children — the
next generation, the ones the systems failed — beginning to study the
laws. This is the awakening Jubilees prophesied a hundred and fifty
years before Yahusha (Jesus) was born. This is what Hosea 3:5 meant.
This is what is happening across the world right now, in homes you have
never visited, in lives you will never know, as the scattered seed
reaches back across the church’s seventeen centuries of mediation, opens
the prophets without the lens, finds the calendar without the liturgical
year laid over it, finds the Sabbath without the moved day, finds the
festivals without the Christianizing labels, and finds their identity as
Yashar’el (Israel) without any of the four replacement readings. The
children are studying the laws. Jubilees called it.

And it says, in chapter 50, the closing chapter, that this entire arc —
from Adam to Sinai to the gathering to the appointed reign — sits inside
a Jubilee architecture. There are forty-nine jubilees from the days of
Adam until this day, the angel of the presence tells Moses, with the
count holding all the way down. The giving of the Torah at Sinai is the
Jubilee of Jubilees from Adam — the great reset, the maximum liberation,
the moment the heavenly architecture lands at full weight on a body just
brought out of bondage. And the Jubilees keep counting. The jubilees
will pass by, until Yashar’el (Israel) is cleansed from all guilt of
fornication, and uncleanness, and pollution, and sin, and error, and
dwells with confidence in all the land, and there will be no more a
Satan or any evil one, and the land will be clean from that time for
evermore. The book opens with the gathering. The book closes with the
gathering. The architecture is internally seamless.

This volume restores Jubilees to the awakening reader the way it
deserves to be restored. The text is R.H. Charles’ 1917 translation —
the same translator whose Enoch you may already have on your shelf —
modernized into present-day English, scrubbed of the apparatus brackets
and obelisks that mark a critical edition rather than serve a reader,
and corrected at the specific places where Charles’ theology imposed
itself on his word choice. The sacred names are restored in the body of
every chapter, with the conventional English in parentheses on every
mention so the reader meeting them for the first time is never lost. The
sustained commentary that follows each chapter is in the voice of the
Remnant of Promise series — patient toward the deceived, plain about the
systems, and never trying to write a rulebook over the reader’s life.
The book’s job is to lift the lie off the text and let Jubilees say what
it actually says. What the reader does with it next is between the
reader and the Father.

A word about the four houses. The horn’s pulpit has spent seventeen
centuries telling the people in the pews that the Sabbath is a Yahudi
(Jewish) ordinance, the festivals are obsolete, the Torah is the curse,
the holy seed of Jacob has been replaced by the church, and the
prophets’ specific promises of restoration have been spiritualized into
a metaphor. None of that is in this book. None of that has ever been in
this book. The grandmothers and grandfathers in the pews who have loved
the Father with what they were given are not the enemies of this book.
They are also the lost sheep. The system that gave them what they were
given is what this book — like every book in this series — exists to
dismantle. The same patience extends to the synagogue, where the body of
Yahudah (Judah) has built its own walls against the plain reading of the
prophets concerning the Messiah (Christ) and the gathering of the
scattered house; to the Hebrew roots and Messianic communities, where
Christian replacement theology often persists in Torah clothing as a
doctrine that anyone who keeps the commandments is thereby Yashar’el
(Israel) regardless of bloodline — a teaching the prophets and Jubilees
both refuse; and to the houses of Islam, where the same denial wears a
different costume. All four houses, in different ways, share one
foundational lie: that there are no scattered tribes coming home, that
the binary is Jew and everybody else, that the prophetic gathering is
finished or transferred or metaphorical or replaced. The lie is the
antichrist. The people inside the houses are victims. Jubilees was set
aside because it makes the lie too plain to maintain. This volume
returns the book to where it has always belonged — in the hands of
awakening believers who are reading the prophets without the lens.

Read it as one continuous piece if you can. The book is short. The arc
is one arc. The gathering at chapter 1 is the gathering at chapter 50,
and the chapters in between are the architecture by which Yahuah (God)
brought the body from Adam to Sinai and is, in this season, bringing the
body from the long exile home. If you have come to this book with the
lens of any of the four houses still on you, the commentary will press
the lens back where it can be removed. If you have already put the lens
down, the commentary will sharpen what you have been seeing. Either way,
the text is the text. The book is older than the things that opposed it.
The witness has not retired. Read.

The Withdrawal at Laodicea

The book you are holding was not lost. The book was withdrawn. There is
a difference, and the difference matters, because the systems that
withdrew it have spent the seventeen centuries since insisting that what
they removed was never canon, was never read in the assembly, was never
quoted by the apostles, was never carried by the patriarchs, was never
given at Sinai inside the same forty days of revelation that produced
the Torah on the tables of stone. Each one of those claims is false.
Jubilees was canon in the assembly that read it. Jubilees was quoted by
the apostolic writings. Jubilees was preserved in the Ethiopic Bible
from the council that withdrew it down to the present day, in continuous
liturgical use, in the only branch of the family that did not let the
horn move it. And Jubilees was confirmed at Qumran in the second half of
the twentieth century by fourteen Hebrew and Aramaic manuscript
witnesses dated to the very window the book itself describes — the
second-century-BCE seam between the close of the Torah's transmission
and the rise of the Hasmonean priesthood. The book was not lost. The
book was taken off the shelf. This essay is the record of who took it
off, and why, and what they had to deny in order to keep it off.

The hinge year is 321. In that year Constantine signed the Sunday law of
the Roman Empire, declaring the venerable day of the sun a day of civic
rest for the cities of the empire, exempting only the agricultural
classes from its requirement. The phrasing is in his own hand. Dies
Solis — the day of the sun — was the day already kept by the Mithraic
and Sol Invictus cults of the imperial military, the day on which
Constantine himself had received his coin-image of the Unconquered Sun a
decade earlier, and the day that had no Sabbath weight in the Torah
Yahuah (God) gave to Moses. The Sabbath of the fourth commandment is the
seventh day. The day Constantine selected was the first day. The motive
for the move is not in dispute among the historians who have read the
imperial correspondence — Constantine wanted a single religious day for
the cities of the empire, and the Christianity he intended to elevate
had been drifting toward Sunday observance under the cumulative pressure
of two centuries of distancing itself from the Sabbath-keeping body that
had birthed it. The 321 edict was not the invention of Sunday
Christianity; it was the legal codification of a drift that had been
happening already inside the assemblies that wanted to be visibly
distinguishable from the Yahudim (Jews) who still kept the seventh day.

Forty-two years later, the Council of Laodicea sat. Its precise date is
debated — somewhere between 363 and 365 — but its decisions are not.
Canon 16 instituted the Gospel reading on the day called Sabbath, which
the council carefully redefined as a Saturday observance permitted to
read but not to rest. Canon 29 spoke plainly: Christians must not
Judaize by resting on the Sabbath, but must work on that day, rather
honouring the Lord's Day; and, if they can, resting then as Christians.
But if any shall be found to be Judaizers, let them be anathema from
Messiah (Christ). The fourth commandment of the Torah Yahuah (God) wrote
with his own finger on stone — anathematized by ecclesiastical decree,
on the authority of the same body that called Yahusha (Jesus) Adonai
(Lord) while disregarding the day Yahusha (Jesus) had kept his entire
earthly walk and the day his apostles continued to keep into Acts and
beyond.

Two canons later, Laodicea addressed the books. Canon 59 forbade the
reading in church of any work not approved by the bishops; canon 60
produced the approved list. Jubilees was not on it. Neither was 1 Enoch.
Neither was Jasher, by whatever name it then carried in the
Greek-speaking churches. The list of withdrawn texts was longer than
these three — but these three travel together, and these three are the
architecture this volume restores. They were not erased. They were not
declared heretical in the usual sense. They were quietly removed from
the public reading, removed from the lectionary, removed from the canon
lists the bishops circulated to the parishes — and within a generation
the laity did not know they had ever been read, because no one was
reading them aloud where the laity sat. That is how a book disappears.
Not by being burned. By being stopped from being heard.

A word about why. Each of the four houses that would later carry the
Jew-and-Gentile binary as a substitute for the prophetic gathering had
its own reason to need Jubilees silenced, and the reasons together
explain why the book has stayed silenced everywhere except inside the
Ethiopian church and inside the Yahudi (Jewish) memory of the
second-temple period that was preserved at Qumran without being
preserved as scripture in the post-Yavneh canon.

Christianity needed Jubilees gone because Jubilees says the Sabbath is
older than Sinai. The book opens at chapter 2 with the angel of the
presence telling Moses that the seventh day was hallowed at creation,
kept by Yahuah (God) himself with the angels of the presence and the
angels of sanctification before any human reception of the law, written
on the heavenly tables as a perpetual ordinance, given to Yashar'el
(Israel) at Sinai not as a new commandment but as the ratification on
earth of an architecture already running in heaven. If the Sabbath is
older than Sinai, the Sabbath cannot have been a covenantal sign tied
only to the Mosaic dispensation, and if the Sabbath is not tied only to
Moses then the horn's argument that the day moved when the Messiah
(Christ) rose collapses on contact with the Torah's own self-witness.
The argument requires Jubilees not to be read. The argument also
requires the Sabbath not to appear in the eternal frame of the new
heavens and the new earth — which is exactly where Isaiah 66:23 places
it, from one Sabbath to another shall all flesh come to worship before
me, says Yahuah (God) — and the argument requires the apostolic Sabbath
observance recorded in Acts 13, 16, 17, and 18 to be read as missionary
outreach rather than as the practice of the apostles themselves. None of
those moves is honest. All of them are required by the relocation.
Jubilees is the witness the relocation cannot survive, and so Jubilees
was withdrawn.

Christianity also needed Jubilees gone because Jubilees says the
calendar is solar, not lunar, and the Easter controversies of the second
through the fourth centuries — the Quartodeciman dispute, the Council of
Nicaea's calendar pronouncements in 325, the long fight over how to
compute the date of the resurrection — would have been resolved on
Yahuah (God)'s own published reckoning had Jubilees been a witness in
the room. Jubilees 6 lays the 364-day calendar out in detail: four
quarters of ninety-one days each, the four cardinal days of the
equinoxes and solstices marking the joints of the year, the festivals
fixed on permanent dates that fall on the same day of the same week year
after year. The calendar is engraven on the heavenly tables. It does not
drift. It is not adjusted by the appearance of the new moon at the close
of a lunar month. It is a sun-counted calendar that puts the festivals
on permanent feet, and it is the calendar Enoch 72 also gives, and it is
the calendar the Mishmarot scrolls at Qumran also give, and it is the
calendar the Hasmonean priesthood walked away from when Hellenistic
pressure made the lunar reckoning of the surrounding cultures more
administratively convenient. Christianity did not produce the lunar
drift. Christianity inherited the lunar drift from the post-Hasmonean
priesthood and then layered Easter Sunday on top of it. But Christianity
did need Jubilees silenced, because Jubilees holds the heavenly receipt
for what was traded away.

Judaism needed Jubilees gone because Jubilees says the festivals were
kept by the patriarchs before Sinai. Abraham keeps the Feast of
Tabernacles at chapter 16 — an act the masoretic Genesis does not record
because Genesis is compressed and Jubilees is the angelic record that
fills in what Genesis does not stop to narrate. Jacob keeps the Feast of
Tabernacles at chapter 32, on the same eighth-day calendar Yahuah (God)
would later codify at Leviticus 23. The Feast of Weeks is named at
chapter 6 as a covenant memorial dating from Noah's covenant after the
flood, kept again by Abraham at chapter 22, instituted on the heavenly
tables at chapter 15. The festivals are not Mosaic innovations. The
festivals are the engraved architecture of heaven made visible in the
seasons of the earth, kept by the elect line from Adam down. If the
festivals are older than Sinai, then the post-Yavneh consolidation of
Yahudim (Jewish) practice around the rabbinic calendar — the move from
the second-temple seven-week chronology to the Hillel II calculated
calendar in the fourth century, the loss of the Yom Teruah / Yom Kippur
/ Sukkot rhythm Jubilees describes as engraved on the tables — is itself
a drift away from a deeper architecture. Judaism's reading of itself as
the singular custodian of the Mosaic covenant cannot fully hold against
a book that locates the covenant's calendar in heaven before Sinai, kept
by the patriarchs in the field, ratified on stone at the mountain. So
Judaism, in the post-Yavneh canon decisions, also did not include
Jubilees among the canonical books. The book survived in Yahudi (Jewish)
hands at Qumran and in the Ethiopian preservation, but not in the canon
the rabbinic tradition carried forward.

The Hebrew roots and Torah-observant communities of the present
awakening need Jubilees too — but they need it on different terms,
because the inherited error in those communities is different. The error
in Hebrew roots is the false inclusion gospel: the teaching that anyone
who keeps the commandments thereby becomes Yashar'el (Israel),
regardless of bloodline, regardless of the prophetic naming of the
scattered tribes, regardless of what the prophets have said about who is
being gathered. Jubilees forecloses that error at chapter 15:30–31 in a
single sentence: over Yashar'el (Israel) He did not appoint any angel or
spirit, for He alone is their ruler. The covenant body is the seed of
Jacob, the twelve tribes through their patriarch, distinct from the
nations who were placed under intermediate authorities, distinct from
Ishmael's line and Esau's line who are blessed in their own measure but
are not the seed of promise. The architecture is paternal blood. The
architecture is named. The replacement that swaps spiritual credential
for paternal seed cannot stand on Jubilees. So the false inclusion
gospel needs Jubilees softened, allegorized, or quietly set aside — and
Hebrew roots communities that have not yet heard Jubilees on its own
terms tend to read it through the same Christian-inclusion lens they
exited the church with. This volume puts Jubilees back in front of the
Torah-observant reader without that lens.

Islam needed Jubilees gone because Jubilees says the seed of promise is
through Isaac and Jacob, not through Ishmael. The chapters that
establish this — chapter 16 with the binding of Isaac as the chosen son,
chapter 19 with Isaac blessing Jacob and the covenant continuing through
the younger, chapter 22 with Abraham's last words pressing the line
through Isaac and through Jacob — are unambiguous. Ishmael is blessed;
Ishmael is fruitful; Ishmael is given his measure of land and his twelve
princes of his own. But Ishmael is not the seed of promise. The covenant
Yahuah (God) cut with Abraham is renewed in Isaac, in Jacob, in the
twelve tribes through Jacob, and the prophetic gathering of Yashar'el
(Israel) is the gathering of those twelve. Islam's transfer of the
covenant to Ishmael cannot survive the book. So the book was never
received in the Arabic translation tradition, and the witness from
Ethiopia did not cross the Red Sea into the Arabian peninsula, and the
silence held.

Four houses. Four denials. Four reasons the book stayed off the shelf
for seventeen centuries. The book itself does not change. The book sat
patiently in the Ethiopian preservation, in continuous liturgical use,
while the four houses sorted out their reasons for leaving it where it
was.

A word about Ethiopia. The Ethiopian Tewahedo Orthodox Church preserved
Jubilees as Maṣḥafa Kufālē — the Book of Division — in continuous
canonical use from the fourth century to the present day. The Ethiopian
canon includes Jubilees alongside 1 Enoch and other books the Western
canons withdrew. The preservation is not an accident of geography. The
Ethiopian church received its scriptures through a route that did not
run through the Greek and Latin western consolidation, and it kept what
the western consolidation set aside. The same preservation runs for 1
Enoch, which the Western academy considered lost until James Bruce
traveled to Abyssinia in 1769 and brought back three Ethiopic
manuscripts that confirmed Jude 1:14–15 had been quoting an actual book
the entire time. Ethiopia kept what Constantine and Laodicea and
Carthage and Trent could not silence in the one place they did not have
authority to reach.

A word about Qumran. Between 1947 and 1956, eleven caves above the
northwest shore of the Dead Sea yielded the manuscript collection of a
second-temple-era Yahudi (Jewish) community that withdrew from the
Hasmonean priesthood and kept its own scriptures in jars sealed against
the Roman destruction of 70 CE. Among those scrolls were fourteen
separate manuscripts of Jubilees, in Hebrew and Aramaic, dated
paleographically to the second and first centuries BCE — older than any
other manuscript witness to the book by more than a thousand years. The
Qumran fragments confirm the book Charles translated from the Ethiopic
against the Hebrew of the second-temple period. The book is not a late
composition. The book is not an Ethiopian invention. The book was
written in Hebrew, kept in Hebrew, copied in Hebrew, and translated into
Greek and into Ge'ez during the centuries when the Septuagint and other
second-temple translations were also being produced. The Western canon's
withdrawal of the book was not a textual judgment. It was an
ecclesiastical decision made on theological convenience, against the
evidence of the textual transmission the rest of the world preserved.

A word about the recovery. The three withdrawn books — 1 Enoch, Jasher,
Jubilees — are returning in the present generation together. James Bruce
brought back Enoch in 1769. The Yashar text was published in Hebrew in
1625 and translated into English in 1840. The Qumran scrolls confirmed
Jubilees in the second half of the twentieth century. The Ethiopic
manuscripts of all three have been collated, photographed, and published
in the academic editions Charles and Knibb and others produced. The
books are in print. The books are searchable. The books are appearing on
the shelves of awakening believers across the world, often within months
of one another, often without the reader having heard of any of them six
months earlier. This is not a publishing trend. This is the second
recovery the prophets named. The pattern Isaiah 11 names — He shall set
up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of
Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah)
from the four corners of the earth — includes the recovery of the
witnesses the long exile silenced. Hosea 4:6 names the mechanism: my
people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. The knowledge is being
restored.

That is what this volume is. It is one of the three books being put back
where they belong, in present-day English, in the restored sacred names,
with the sustained commentary on every chapter the awakening reader
needs in order to hear what the book is actually saying after seventeen
centuries of being told the book did not exist. The volume does not
claim the book is more than it is. The book is a second-temple-era
angelic re-narration of Genesis and the early chapters of Exodus,
presented as the testimony delivered to Moses on Mount Sinai during the
same forty days that produced the tables of stone. The book reads as
scripture in the assemblies that received it as scripture. The book
reads as a parallel witness in the assemblies that did not. Either way,
the book speaks. It speaks loudly enough that four houses spent
seventeen centuries keeping it off the public reading. It speaks loudly
enough that Ethiopia would not let it be moved. It speaks loudly enough
that the Qumran scribes copied it fourteen times. It is speaking loudly
enough now that you have it in your hand.

Read it. The horn moved many things. The horn did not move the heavenly
tables. Jubilees is the receipt.

The Calendar of Heaven

When the angel of the presence speaks at chapter 6 of Jubilees, the
angel does not propose a calendar. The angel does not draft a calendar.
The angel reports a calendar that was already running, engraven on the
heavenly tables, kept by Yahuah (God) himself in the order he had
appointed before the foundation of the earth, given to Noah at the close
of the flood as the ratification on earth of an architecture already
running in heaven. The calendar Jubilees 6 publishes is three hundred
and sixty-four days, divided into four quarters of ninety-one days each,
with four cardinal days at the joints of the quarters where the
equinoxes and the solstices fall, and the festivals fixed on permanent
dates that recur on the same day of the same week year after year for as
long as the earth turns. This is not the calendar the modern reader
knows. This is not the calendar the rabbinic synagogue keeps. This is
not the calendar Constantine and Nicaea deployed for the date of Easter.
It is older than all three. It was given before any of them. It was lost
in the drift the prophets named, and it is being recovered in the season
the prophets also named.

The chapter opens at the third month of the first year after the flood,
with Noah keeping the Feast of Weeks for the first time after the waters
had subsided. The festival is described as a covenant memorial — and
they renewed the festival on the Mount of the new month, and Noah and
his sons made the festival of the seventh week with their children and
the angels of the presence, says verse 21 — and the angel then turns to
Moses and lays out the architecture in detail. Command the children of
Yashar'el (Israel) to observe the years according to this reckoning —
three hundred and sixty-four days, and these will constitute a complete
year, and they will not disturb its time from its days and from its
feasts; for everything will fall out in them according to their
testimony, and they will not leave out any day nor disturb any feasts.
The verb is disturb. The architecture has a fixed shape. To deviate from
the reckoning is to disturb the festivals. The angel anticipates the
deviation. The angel names what will happen when humanity loses the
count: and there will be those who will examine the moon — for it will
disturb the seasons and come from year to year ten days too soon. For
this reason the years will come on them when they will disturb the
order, and make an abominable day the day of testimony, and an unclean
day a feast day, and they will confound all the days, the holy with the
unclean, and the unclean day with the holy; for they will go wrong as to
the months and Sabbaths and feasts and jubilees.

The prophecy has come to pass. The lunar reckoning the angel warned
against became the operating calendar of the post-Hasmonean priesthood,
was carried into the Hillel II calculated calendar of the fourth
century, and has determined the rabbinic festival calendar from that
century to the present. The lunar months drift against the solar year by
approximately eleven days per cycle. The drift is corrected periodically
by the insertion of an intercalary thirteenth month, but the correction
is reactive — it adjusts the calendar after the drift has accumulated,
rather than anchoring the festivals to the fixed solar architecture
Jubilees describes. The result is what the angel said it would be. The
festivals fall on different days of the week year after year. The
Passover lands on a Thursday in one year, a Saturday in the next, a
Tuesday in the year after that. The Feast of Weeks slides. Yom Teruah
and Yom Kippur and the Feast of Tabernacles drift. The day of testimony
— the seventh-day Sabbath of the fourth commandment — remains fixed at
the seventh day of the week, but the festivals it joins to no longer
fall on their permanent appointed places in the architecture, because
the architecture has been replaced.

A word about what the architecture actually is. Jubilees 6 and Enoch 72
give the same calendar. They give it from different angles — Jubilees
gives it as the angel speaking to Moses about the testimony engraven on
the tables, Enoch gives it as the heavenly tour Enoch took with the
angel Uriel through the gates of heaven through which the sun rises and
sets across the year — but the count is identical. Three hundred and
sixty-four days. Four quarters of ninety-one days each. The four
cardinal days fall outside the count of the months: at the spring
equinox, the summer solstice, the autumn equinox, and the winter
solstice, marking the joints between quarters and not assigned to any
month. Each quarter is composed of three months: the first and second
months of the quarter are thirty days each, the third month of the
quarter is thirty-one days, and the cardinal day completes the
ninety-one. Four times ninety-one is three hundred and sixty-four. The
architecture is regular. The architecture is permanent. The festivals
fall on dates that recur on the same day of the same week year after
year. The Passover, fixed at the fourteenth day of the first month,
falls on a Tuesday evening every year. The Feast of Weeks, counted seven
sabbaths after the morrow of the Passover Sabbath, falls on a Sunday
every year. The Feast of Tabernacles, fixed at the fifteenth day of the
seventh month, falls on a Wednesday every year. The Day of Atonement on
the tenth day of the seventh month falls on a Friday every year. The
architecture is the architecture. It does not slide.

The objection lands immediately. A solar year is not three hundred and
sixty-four days. A solar year is approximately three hundred and
sixty-five days and a quarter, and the earth's orbit does not stop after
three hundred and sixty-four. The astronomer presses the question, the
modern reader presses the question, and the answer Jubilees gives is a
doubled answer. The first part of the answer is in the architecture
itself. Three hundred and sixty-four divides cleanly by seven. There are
exactly fifty-two seven-day weeks in a year of three hundred and
sixty-four days. There are exactly seven jubilees of seven seven-week
years in the cycle Jubilees describes. The integer count is not an
astronomical accident; it is a covenantal architecture engineered around
the seventh-day rhythm Yahuah (God) hallowed at creation. A calendar
built on three hundred and sixty-four days places every festival on a
permanent day of the week, never on a Sabbath, never displacing a
Sabbath, never asking the body to choose between the festival and the
day Yahuah (God) had hallowed. The lunar calendar cannot do this. The
Gregorian calendar cannot do this. Only the
three-hundred-and-sixty-four-day reckoning can do this, and that is the
reckoning Jubilees 6 publishes as the engraved architecture of heaven.

The second part of the answer is in the Qumran witness. The Mishmarot
scrolls — the calendrical texts found at Qumran, including 4Q319 through
4Q321 and 4Q325 — preserve a working application of the
three-hundred-and-sixty-four-day calendar across the second-temple
period, with the priestly courses of 1 Chronicles 24 rotated through the
year on a fixed cycle that produces a six-year repetition pattern. The
community at Qumran was not theorizing the calendar. The community was
using it. The scrolls record the Sabbaths and festivals on which each
priestly course served, year after year, decade after decade, in a
continuous calendrical practice that ran in parallel to the lunar
reckoning the temple in Jerusalem had adopted. The withdrawal from the
temple priesthood was, in part, a withdrawal over the calendar. The
community at Qumran considered the temple priesthood to have abandoned
the engraved reckoning and to have taken up an abominable substitute.
The framing is sharp, and the framing is from a Yahudi (Jewish)
community of the second century BCE that read Jubilees and 1 Enoch as
scripture and kept the calendar both books published. The drift the
angel of the presence warned about in Jubilees 6 was already, by the
second century BCE, the operating calendar of the Hellenistic-pressured
priesthood. The Qumran community did not invent the protest. The Qumran
community joined the witness Jubilees and Enoch had been making for
centuries.

The drift to the lunar reckoning was not the only drift. By the fourth
century of the present era, the rabbinic authority Hillel II had
codified the calculated lunar-and-intercalary calendar that the Yahudim
(Jewish) communities of the diaspora keep to the present day. The Hillel
II calendar is not the calendar of Jubilees, and it is not the calendar
of the second-temple period. It is a fourth-century rabbinic
systematization of the lunar reckoning the post-Hasmonean priesthood had
adopted, normalized to a calculated nineteen-year cycle that adds an
intercalary month seven times in the cycle to keep the lunar months from
drifting too far against the solar year. The calendar is
administratively elegant. The calendar is also explicitly disconnected
from the engraved architecture Jubilees gave to Noah. The Yahudim
(Jewish) believer who keeps the festivals on Hillel II is keeping
festivals — and the keeping is not nothing — but the calendar the
believer is keeping is not the calendar engraved on the heavenly tables.
It is the calendar the rabbinic tradition assembled in the centuries
after the temple fell, as a way of preserving the festivals in the
absence of a temple priesthood that could observe the new moons in the
prescribed way.

Christianity inherited the lunar drift through a different route, and
applied a different solution. The early assemblies that observed the
Passover did so on the fourteenth day of the lunar first month, in
agreement with the Yahudi (Jewish) practice of the period — this is the
Quartodeciman tradition that ran into the second and third centuries,
especially in the assemblies of Asia Minor under the leadership of
teachers like Polycarp who had received the practice through John the
apostle. The Quartodeciman position was that the Passover was the
Passover, kept on the fourteenth day of the first month regardless of
which day of the week that fell on, in continuity with the calendar
Yahuah (God) had given. The opposing position, which prevailed in Rome
and was eventually imposed across the empire by the post-Nicene Easter
computation, was that the resurrection should be commemorated on a
Sunday, and that the date of the commemoration should be the first
Sunday after the first full moon after the spring equinox. The
computation is a Christian-Roman lunar-solar hybrid. It has nothing in
common with the Jubilees architecture. It does not put the Passover on
the fourteenth of the first month. It does not put any festival on a
permanent date. It floats Easter across a five-week window from late
March to late April, year after year, with the bishops of the major sees
publishing the date in advance to the parishes — a practice that
continues in the Western and Eastern churches to the present day. The
believer who keeps the Easter date is not keeping the Passover. The
believer is keeping a fourth-century ecclesiastical computation that was
constructed precisely to disambiguate the Christian observance from the
Yahudi (Jewish) one and to preserve the visibility of the
Sunday-resurrection emphasis the relocation of the Sabbath had already
established.

The Gregorian calendar, promulgated by Pope Gregory XIII in 1582 and
adopted across the Western world in the centuries that followed,
completed the architectural separation. The Gregorian reform was not
concerned with festival placement. The reform was concerned with the
spring equinox, which had drifted ten days against the Julian calendar
over the millennium since Nicaea, and with restoring the equinox to the
date the Easter computation required. The reform did its job. The reform
also moved the cardinal day. The spring equinox is now fixed in the
Gregorian system at March 20 or March 21. The architecture Jubilees 6
gave Noah does not run on the Gregorian calendar at all. The two
calendars are doing different work. The Gregorian calendar is a
civil-administrative reckoning of the solar year, with months of
irregular length (twenty-eight, thirty, thirty-one days) inherited from
Roman administrative practice and retained for inertia. The Jubilees
calendar is a covenantal architecture of festival placement, with months
of regular length (thirty, thirty, thirty-one) keyed to the four
quarters and the four cardinal days. The Gregorian calendar tells you
what day to file your taxes. The Jubilees calendar tells you when the
Father said to come up to the mountain.

A word about what was lost when the calendar drifted. The festivals lost
their permanent days of the week. The Sabbath retained its place — the
seventh day is still the seventh day, and the lunar drift does not move
it — but the festivals it was supposed to anchor began to fall sometimes
on Sabbath itself, sometimes on the day before, sometimes on the day
after, in a sliding pattern that broke the architectural relationship
the engraved tables had given. The Feast of Weeks lost its Sunday
placement. The Passover Sabbath, which Jubilees and the Qumran calendar
both place on a fixed Wednesday, became a sliding date in both the
Yahudi (Jewish) reckoning and the Christian one. The patriarchal pattern
Jubilees describes — Abraham keeping the Feast of Tabernacles on the
same fixed date Adam had kept it, Isaac keeping the Feast of Weeks on
the same fixed date Noah had kept it, Jacob keeping the eighth day of
Tabernacles on the same fixed date the heavenly tables described —
became impossible to recover, because the calendar the patriarchs had
used was no longer running in either house. The architecture had been
substituted. The body had to choose between the calendar the rabbis
published and the calendar the bishops published, and neither was the
calendar Yahuah (God) had given Noah. Both were drift.

A word about what is being recovered. The Qumran scrolls were sealed in
the jars during the long withdrawal, and the jars were opened in the
second half of the twentieth century, and the calendar of Jubilees 6
came up out of the cave with the rest of the scrolls. The scholarly
editions are now in print. The calendrical texts have been studied for
seventy years, and the seventeen-year project of editing 4Q319 (the Otot
— the signs scroll, which lays out the priestly-course rotation across a
complete jubilee cycle) has been completed and published. The
architecture is no longer hidden. The body that wants to know the
calendar Yahuah (God) gave Noah can read Jubilees 6 and Enoch 72 and the
Mishmarot side by side and see what was given before either drift. The
recovery is happening across the same window in which the Sabbath itself
is being recovered by awakening believers across the world who had been
keeping Sunday and have come back to the seventh day. The two recoveries
belong to each other. The day Yahuah (God) hallowed and the calendar
Yahuah (God) engraved are one architecture. The body that keeps the day
will, in time, also be drawn into the architecture the day belongs
inside. The book does not assign that drawing. The book lays the witness
out and lets the Father lead.

What this volume does with the calendar is what the volume does with
everything else. It gives you the chapter as it stands. It does not tell
you what to do with the chapter. The commentary at chapter 6 of this
volume sets the architecture out in detail — the four quarters, the
cardinal days, the priestly-course rotation, the loss and the recovery.
The commentary does not tell the reader to abandon the calendar the
reader is currently keeping. The commentary does not prescribe a switch.
The commentary trusts the Father with the unfolding. The reader who has
just learned that the Sabbath was hallowed at creation, kept by the
angels in heaven before any human reception, and never moved by Yahuah
(God) — that reader, given a few months and the leading of the Ruach
HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), will be drawn toward the day. The reader who has
just learned that the festivals were kept by the patriarchs before Sinai
on a fixed solar architecture engraven on the heavenly tables — that
reader, in time, will begin to ask what the architecture asks of them.
The book does not need to answer the question for the reader. The Father
knows the reader's name. The Father will lead.

What this volume affirms is that the architecture is real. The calendar
of heaven is the calendar of heaven. It is engraven. It does not move.
It was published in Jubilees 6 and in Enoch 72 and in the Mishmarot
scrolls and in the Ethiopic preservation, and it has been waiting for
the body that wants to read it. The horn moved many things. The horn did
not move the cardinal days. The equinoxes still fall where they fall.
The solstices still fall where they fall. The Sabbath still falls on the
seventh day. The festivals still belong to the architecture they were
given inside. The body that has been awakened to the day Yahuah (God)
hallowed will be awakened, in due season, to the calendar the day
belongs inside. The book is here for that season.

Read chapter 6 carefully when you reach it. The architecture is in the
chapter. The commentary at chapter 6 in this volume traces it. The
chapter itself does the work the chapter was given to do, which is to
publish the engraved reckoning so the body that has lost it can find it
again.

A Note on the Translation

This volume is built on R.H. Charles’ 1917 translation of the Book of
Jubilees, prepared from the Ethiopic manuscripts that were the only
complete witness to the book until the Qumran scrolls confirmed
substantial portions of the Hebrew original almost half a century later.
Charles’ Jubilees was the same kind of accomplishment as his Enoch — a
careful, scholarly, public-domain edition that put the book in front of
English readers in a form scholars could trust and laypersons could
read. This volume keeps Charles as the base for the same reason the
Enoch volume in this series keeps him as the base: a single translator
across the two books, a consistent voice, a consistent ear, and a level
of scholarship that has not been bettered in any subsequent
public-domain edition. What Charles did, this volume does not undo. What
Charles did with his theology in his hand, this volume gently corrects.

The work of preparation passed through four passes before a single word
of commentary was written. The first pass took Charles’ edition from the
original sacred-texts.com transcription, stripped the page-break
markers, the OCR artifacts, and the apparatus footnotes that belonged to
the critical edition rather than to the reader’s volume, and produced a
clean text. The second pass modernized the English. Charles wrote in the
King James register that was still standard in 1917 — thou, thee, thy,
thine, ye, hast, saith, cometh — and the awakening reader of this volume
is meeting the book in present-day English. Thou hast becomes you have.
Saith becomes says. Cometh becomes comes. Wast becomes were. Unto
becomes to. The voice does not change; the obstacle is removed. Where
Charles’ marginal A.M. (Anno Mundi) date annotations interrupted the
body text, those were stripped — the chronology Jubilees gives in its
own jubilee and week of years counts is the chronology the book wants
the reader to keep.

The third pass restored the sacred names. Every occurrence of the Lord,
Lord, and the LORD in the body text was restored to Yahuah (God), with
the parenthetical on every mention. God was restored to Elohim (God).
Most High was restored to El Elyon (Most High). Almighty — the two
occurrences underlying the Hebrew El Shaddai — was restored to El
Shaddai (God Almighty), matching the convention used for restored divine
titles. The covenant people-names followed the same rule: Israel became
Yashar’el (Israel); Judah became Yahudah (Judah); the related forms
(Israel’s, Judah’s) carried the possessive on both the restored name and
the conventional translation. Every other biblical human name and city
name — Jacob, Isaac, Abraham, Moses, Joseph, Adam, Eve, Noah, Shem,
Bethel, Hebron, Mount Sinai, Mount Zion, Egypt — remains in the
conventional English the reader knows by sight. The retention mechanism
is reserved for the Deity and for the covenant body the prophets traced
and promised to gather. Restoring every Hebrew patriarchal name would
raise the entry cost on the reader without carrying the
third-commandment weight that Yahuah and Yahusha carry, and without
naming the covenant body the way Yashar’el, Yahudah, and Yahudim do. The
convention is the convention used in the published Ephraim Rising, in
the published Enoch volume of this series, and in the Jasher volume. It
is consistent across the body of work.

The fourth pass corrected Charles where his theology imposed on his word
choice. Five categories of correction were applied. The work was not
aggressive — the goal is name restoration, not retranslation — but at
the places where Charles’ theology was visible in his English, the
imposition was lifted.

First, Gentiles and Gentile were replaced with the nations. There are
twenty-three occurrences of Gentiles or Gentile in Charles’ Jubilees.
Every one of them refers to non-covenant peoples in a pre-Pauline frame
— the heathen kingdoms among whom Yashar’el (Israel) is scattered as
judgment, the nations Yashar’el (Israel) is warned against imitating,
the non-elect line of Abraham’s other sons. None of these are the
Pauline scattered-seed references where Gentiles (uncircumcision, the
nations) is the apostolic shorthand for the lost sheep of the house of
Yashar’el (Israel) living as foreigners among the nations of their
dispersion. Jubilees pre-dates Paul by a century and a half, and the
term in its source is the Hebrew goyim — the nations. Charles rendered
it Gentiles because that was the standard English word in 1917. The
standard English word in 1917 was already, by then, soaked through with
Christian replacement theology that read Gentiles as the third category
of person who replaced Yashar’el (Israel) in the new dispensation.
Restoring the nations puts the word back where it was always meant to be
— naming the third category of the framework, the peoples Yahuah (God)
divided in chapter 9 and held distinct from the covenant body across the
rest of the book.

Second, Charles’ apparatus brackets and obelisk pairs were stripped.
Charles’ 1917 edition was a critical edition for scholars: square
brackets marked phrases supplied from variant Ethiopic manuscripts that
the main manuscript had lost; daggers (†…†) marked phrases Charles
emended on his own judgment to repair what he believed were scribal
corruptions. Forty-eight bracketed insertions and forty-nine
dagger-marked emendations existed in his text. In a critical edition for
textual scholars, that apparatus is appropriate. In a reader’s volume
for awakening believers, it is noise. The stripping does not change a
single word of Charles’ best reading; it removes the marks that would
distract the reader who is not engaged in textual criticism. The same
posture was used in the Enoch and Jasher volumes of this series.

Third, the four places where Charles supplied a parenthetical (God) to
clarify an ambiguous pronoun antecedent in his Greek and Ethiopic source
were restored to the full Elohim (God), matching the surrounding
restored body. The supplied subject was Charles’ service to the reader;
restoring it consistently keeps the body of the text uniform.

Fourth, a single capitalized Spirit in chapter 1, verse 21 — Moses’
prayer, create in them a clean heart and a holy Spirit — was normalized
to lowercase spirit to match the parallel verse in 1:23, where Charles
himself used holy spirit in lowercase. Both verses describe the human
spirit being made holy, not the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) as a divine
person. Charles’ inconsistency was a typographical accident, not a
theological claim. The lowercase form is what the parallel verse already
established.

Fifth, ten OCR page-number artifacts (p. 60, p. 70, etc.) and one missed
paragraph break that broke the compound name the Lord my God across
chapter 45 verse 3 were repaired. The page-numbers were vestiges of the
sacred-texts.com layout that had leaked through the original cleanup;
the paragraph break was an OCR misreading that had defeated the
name-restoration regex. Both are pure typography. Both are gone.

A note on what was not changed. Charles’ word choices outside these five
categories are kept. Where his English is archaic-feeling but accurate
to the source, it stands. Where his sentence structure is dense, it
stands. Where his rendering of an obscure phrase is debatable, it
stands. The reader who wants to dispute a particular word can go to the
original. This volume’s job is not to retranslate Jubilees. This
volume’s job is to put Charles’ careful work in front of the reader with
the names restored, the apparatus removed, the present-day English in
place, and the specific theological impositions corrected at the places
where they would clog the reading. Everything else is Charles, and
Charles deserves the credit.

A note on the chapter and verse divisions. The chapter divisions follow
Charles’ fifty-chapter structure, which itself follows the standard
division of the Ethiopic and the Latin fragments. The verse divisions
inside each chapter are also Charles’ — they correspond to the standard
reference numbering that scholars and translators have used for the book
since the late nineteenth century. When the commentary refers to
Jubilees 6:17 or chapter 23:26, the reference points to Charles’ verse
and the equivalent verse in any other modern Jubilees translation the
reader may have on the shelf.

A note on the relation to other translations. The reader may be aware
that other public-domain English translations of Jubilees exist — most
notably George H. Schodde’s 1888 edition, which is more literal in
places and contains fewer interpretive parentheticals than Charles.
Schodde was consulted at the corrections pass, particularly at the four
bare (God) insertions and at the Gentiles / the nations decision. Where
Charles’ rendering reflected a defensible interpretive choice that was
not theologically loaded, Charles was kept for the consistency of voice
across this series. Where Charles’ rendering reflected an imposition
Schodde did not share, the imposition was lifted in this volume’s text
and the reasoning was logged.

The reader who wants to compare. The Charles 1917 source text, the
Schodde 1888 alternative, and the corrections log for this volume are
all in the public domain or are part of the working notes that produced
this book. Anyone who wishes to verify a specific word, a specific
verse, or a specific correction can do so. Nothing in this volume is
hidden. The work was done in the open. The book is ancient. The work to
recover it is not finished. The reader is welcome to keep digging.

The corrections do not amount to a new translation. The corrections
amount to a careful editorial pass over Charles’ work that removes the
apparatus, restores the names, modernizes the English, and lifts the few
specific impositions that would otherwise sit in the reader’s path. What
remains is Jubilees, in Charles’ voice, with the names of the Father and
of the covenant body restored to where they belong, and with the
sustained commentary on every chapter the awakening reader needs in
order to hear what the book actually says.

The names of the Father, of the Son, and of the body the prophets traced
are not decorative. They are the load. Restoring them in this volume is
the editorial work that lets the rest of the book do what it was given
to do. Tremble at his Word. The book is in your hands.

chapters.title: The Revelation at Sinai

verses.text: This is the history of the division of the days of the law and of the testimony, of the events of the years, of their (year) weeks, of their jubilees throughout all the years of the world, as Yahuah (God) spake to Moses on Mount Sinai when he went up to receive the tables of the law and of the commandment, according to the voice of Elohim (God) as He said to him, “Go up to the top of the Mount.” And it came to pass in the first year of the exodus of the children of Yashar’el (Israel) out of Egypt, in the third month, on the sixteenth day of the month, that Elohim (God) spake to Moses, saying: “Come up to Me on the Mount, and I will give you two tables of stone of the law and of the commandment, which I have written, that you may teach them.”
And Moses went up into the mount of Elohim (God), and the glory of Yahuah (God) abode on Mount Sinai, and a cloud overshadowed it six days.
And He called to Moses on the seventh day out of the midst of the cloud, and the appearance of the glory of Yahuah (God) was like a flaming fire on the top of the Mount.
And Moses was on the Mount forty days and forty nights, and Elohim (God) taught him the earlier and the later history of the division of all the days of the law and of the testimony.

And He said: "Incline your heart to every word which I shall speak to you on this Mount, and write them in a book in order that their generations may see how I have not forsaken them for all the evil which they have wrought in transgressing the covenant which I establish between Me and you for their generations this day on Mount Sinai. And thus it will come to pass when all these things come upon them, that they will recognize that I am more righteous than they in all their judgments and in all their actions, and they will recognize that I have been truly with them.

And do you write for yourself all these words which I declare to you this day, for I know their rebellion and their stiff neck, before I bring them into the land of which I sware to their fathers, to Abraham and to Isaac and to Jacob, saying: “To your seed will I give a land flowing with milk and honey.

And they will eat and be satisfied, and they will turn to strange gods, to (gods) which cannot deliver them from aught of their tribulation:”and this witness shall be heard for a witness against them.

For they will forget all My commandments, (even) all that I command them, and they will walk after the nations, and after their uncleanness, and after their shame, and will serve their gods, and these will prove to them an offence and a tribulation and an affliction and a snare.

And many will perish and they will be taken captive, and will fall into the hands of the enemy, because they have forsaken My ordinances and My commandments, and the festivals of My covenant, and My sabbaths, and My holy place which I have hallowed for Myself in their midst, and My tabernacle, and My sanctuary, which I have hallowed for Myself in the midst of the land, that I should set My name upon it, and that it should dwell (there). And they will make to themselves high places and groves and graven images, and they will worship, each his own (graven image), so as to go astray, and they will sacrifice their children to demons, and to all the works of the error of their hearts.

And I will send witnesses to them, that I may witness against them, but they will not hear, and will slay the witnesses also, and they will persecute those who seek the law, and they will abrogate and change everything so as to work evil before My eyes.

And I shall hide My face from them, and I shall deliver them into the hand of the nations for captivity, and for a prey, and for devouring, and I shall remove them from the midst of the land, and I shall scatter them amongst the nations.
And they will forget all My law and all My commandments and all My judgments, and will go astray as to new moons, and sabbaths, and festivals, and jubilees, and ordinances.

And after this they will turn to Me from amongst the nations with all their heart and with all their soul and with all their strength, and I shall gather them from amongst all the nations, and they will seek Me, so that I shall be found of them, when they seek Me with all their heart and with all their soul. And I shall disclose to them abounding peace with righteousness, and I shall remove them the plant of uprightness, with all My heart and with all My soul, and they will be for a blessing and not for a curse, and they will be the head and not the tail.
And I shall build My sanctuary in their midst, and I shall dwell with them, and I shall be their Elohim (God) and they will be My people in truth and righteousness.
And I shall not forsake them nor fail them; for I am Yahuah their Elohim (the LORD their God)."

And Moses fell on his face and prayed and said, "O Yahuah (God) my Elohim (God), do not forsake Your people and Your inheritance, so that they should wander in the error of their hearts, and do not deliver them into the hands of their enemies, the nations, lest they should rule over them and cause them to sin against You.

Let Your mercy, O Yahuah (God), be lifted up upon Your people, and create in them an upright spirit, and let not the spirit of Beliar rule over them to accuse them before You, and to ensnare them from all the paths of righteousness, so that they may perish from before Your face. But they are Your people and Your inheritance, which You have delivered with Your great power from the hands of the Egyptians: create in them a clean heart and a holy spirit, and let them not be ensnared in their sins from henceforth until eternity."
And Yahuah (God) said to Moses: "I know their contrariness and their thoughts and their stiffneckedness, and they will not be obedient till they confess their own sin and the sin of their fathers.

And after this they will turn to Me in all uprightness and with all (their) heart and with all (their) soul, and I shall circumcise the foreskin of their heart and the foreskin of the heart of their seed, and I shall create in them a holy spirit, and I shall cleanse them so that they shall not turn away from Me from that day to eternity.
And their souls will cleave to Me and to all My commandments, and they will fulfil My commandments, and I shall be their Father and they will be My children.

And they will all be called children of the living Elohim (God), and every angel and every spirit will know, yea, they will know that these are My children, and that I am their Father in uprightness and righteousness, and that I love them. And do you write down for yourself all these words which I declare to you on this mountain, the first and the last, which shall come to pass in all the divisions of the days in the law and in the testimony and in the weeks and the jubilees to eternity, until I descend and dwell with them throughout eternity." And He said to the angel of the presence: “Write for Moses from the beginning of creation till My sanctuary has been built among them for all eternity.

And Yahuah (God) will appear to the eyes of all, and all will know that I am the Elohim (God) of Yashar’el (Israel) and the Father of all the children of Jacob, and King on Mount Zion for all eternity. And Zion and Jerusalem will be holy.”

And the angel of the presence who went before the camp of Yashar’el (Israel) took the tables of the divisions of the years –from the time of the creation–of the law and of the testimony of the weeks, of the jubilees, according to the individual years, according to all the number of the jubilees according to the individual years, from the day of the new creation when the heavens and the earth shall be renewed and all their creation according to the powers of the heaven, and according to all the creation of the earth, until the sanctuary of Yahuah (God) shall be made in Jerusalem on Mount Zion, and all the luminaries be renewed for healing and for peace and for blessing for all the elect of Yashar’el (Israel), and that thus it may be from that day and to all the days of the earth.

chapters.commentary: The book opens at Sinai, in the third month of the first year of the exodus, on the sixteenth day. The angel of the presence is told to write — not because the words are new, but because they were already true and Moses was brought up the mountain to receive what heaven had been holding. The frame is set before a single line of creation is recounted: this is a book of the division of the days, the appointed weeks of years, the jubilees ordered from before the foundation. Yahuah (God) is not improvising. The calendar is not arbitrary. The covenant is not a contingency. What Moses is about to receive is the structure already engraved on the heavenly tables, and the book closes the gap between what heaven has and what the earth has been given. The chapter’s first hard word is not flattering. Yahuah (God) tells Moses, in the same breath as he gives the tables, that the people will turn to strange gods, walk after the nations, sacrifice their children to demons, and abandon the festivals and the sabbaths and the holy place (i. 8–11). Read this with the inherited Christian lens — the lens that says the Torah was a temporary tutor, the festivals were shadows, the sabbath was a foreshadow of something later abolished — and the verse contradicts itself: how can a people forget something that is going to be abolished? The lens fails the text. Read it the way Jubilees actually means it, and the verse is straightforward: the festivals, the sabbaths, the holy place, the sanctuary — these are the inheritance the people will forsake. And precisely because they are the inheritance, Yahuah (God) calls forsaking them a covenant breach. The chapter’s second hard word is the prophecy of the gathering. Verses 15–18 are not vague. Yahuah (God) says he will gather them from amongst all the nations after they turn to him with all their heart and soul; he will disclose abounding peace with righteousness; he will plant them as the plant of uprightness; he will build his sanctuary in their midst; he will be their Elohim (God) and they will be his people in truth and righteousness. This is the same gathering Jeremiah 16, Isaiah 11, Ezekiel 36–37, Hosea 1–2, and Zechariah 10 announce — the gathering of the paternal blood remnant of all twelve tribes, the gathering Christianity has spent seventeen centuries spiritualizing into a metaphor for the church and that modern Judaism has spent its own centuries collapsing into the return of Yahudim (Jews) alone. Jubilees opens with neither move. The book opens inside the prophetic restoration the houses deny. The chapter ends with what verse 23 promises: Yahuah (God) will circumcise the foreskin of their heart and the foreskin of the heart of their seed. The phrase is not Pauline first; it is Mosaic first (Deuteronomy 30:6), and Jubilees stations it here at the beginning of the book to mark what the new covenant of Jeremiah 31 actually does — Torah written on the heart by the Spirit. Not Torah replaced. Not Torah retired. Torah internalized, by the work of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), in a people whose stiff necks have been broken by exile and whose hearts have been opened by the gathering. This is the spine of the entire book, planted in the first chapter: Yahuah (God) does not abandon what he hallowed. He gathers what he scattered and writes his law on what he has cleaned. The chapter closes with the angel of the presence taking the tables of the divisions of the years. The framing matters: what follows is not a parallel Genesis. It is the angelic record of what creation, the patriarchs, and the calendar look like read from the heavenly tables down — not from human memory up.

chapters.title: The Creation and the Sabbath

verses.text: And the angel of the presence spake to Moses according to the word of Yahuah (God), saying: Write the complete history of the creation, how in six days Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) finished all His works and all that He created, and kept Sabbath on the seventh day and hallowed it for all ages, and appointed it as a sign for all His works.

For on the first day He created the heavens which are above and the earth and the waters and all the spirits which serve before Him–the angels of the presence, and the angels of sanctification, and the angels of the spirit of fire and the angels of the spirit of the winds, and the angels of the spirit of the clouds, and of darkness, and of snow and of hail and of hoar frost, and the angels of the voices and of the thunder and of the lightning, and the angels of the spirits of cold and of heat, and of winter and of spring and of autumn and of summer, and of all the spirits of His creatures which are in the heavens and on the earth, (He created) the abysses and the darkness, eventide (and night), and the light, dawn and day, which He has prepared in the knowledge of His heart.
And thereupon we saw His works, and praised Him, and lauded before Him on account of all His works; for seven great works did He create on the first day.

And on the second day He created the firmament in the midst of the waters, and the waters were divided on that day–half of them went up above and half of them went down below the firmament (that was) in the midst over the face of the whole earth. And this was the only work Elohim (God) created on the second day.
And on the third day He commanded the waters to pass from off the face of the whole earth into one place, and the dry land to appear.

And the waters did so as He commanded them, and they retired from off the face of the earth into one place outside of this firmament, and the dry land appeared. And on that day He created for them all the seas according to their separate gathering-places, and all the rivers, and the gatherings of the waters in the mountains and on all the earth, and all the lakes, and all the dew of the earth, and the seed which is sown, and all sprouting things, and fruit-bearing trees, and trees of the wood, and the garden of Eden, in Eden, and all (plants after their kind). These four great works Elohim (God) created on the third day.

And on the fourth day He created the sun and the moon and the stars, and set them in the firmament of the heaven, to give light upon all the earth, and to rule over the day and the night, and divide the light from the darkness.

And Elohim (God) appointed the sun to be a great sign on the earth for days and for sabbaths and for months and for feasts and for years and for sabbaths of years and for jubilees and for all seasons of the years.
And it divides the light from the darkness and for prosperity, that all things may prosper which shoot and grow on the earth. These three kinds He made on the fourth day.

And on the fifth day He created great sea monsters in the depths of the waters, for these were the first things of flesh that were created by His hands, the fish and everything that moves in the waters, and everything that flies, the birds and all their kind. And the sun rose above them to prosper (them), and above everything that was on the earth, everything that shoots out of the earth, and all fruit-bearing trees, and all flesh. These three kinds He created on the fifth day.
And on the sixth day He created all the animals of the earth, and all cattle, and everything that moves on the earth.

And after all this He created man, a man and a woman created He them, and gave him dominion over all that is upon the earth, and in the seas, and over everything that flies, and over beasts and over cattle, and over everything that moves on the earth, and over the whole earth, and over all this He gave him dominion. And these four kinds He created on the sixth day.
And there were altogether two and twenty kinds.

And He finished all His work on the sixth day–all that is in the heavens and on the earth, and in the seas and in the abysses, and in the light and in the darkness, and in everything. And He gave us a great sign, the Sabbath day, that we should work six days, but keep Sabbath on the seventh day from all work.
And all the angels of the presence, and all the angels of sanctification, these two great classes–He has hidden us to keep the Sabbath with Him in heaven and on earth.

And He said to us: “Behold, I will separate to Myself a people from among all the peoples, and these will keep the Sabbath day, and I will sanctify them to Myself as My people, and will bless them; as I have sanctified the Sabbath day and do sanctify (it) to Myself, even so shall I bless them, and they will be My people and I shall be their Elohim (God).

And I have chosen the seed of Jacob from amongst all that I have seen, and have written him down as My firstborn son, and have sanctified him to Myself for ever and ever; and I will teach them the Sabbath day, that they may keep Sabbath thereon from all work.”

And thus He created therein a sign in accordance with which they should keep Sabbath with us on the seventh day, to eat and to drink, and to bless Him who has created all things as He has blessed and sanctified to Himself a peculiar people above all peoples, and that they should keep Sabbath together with us. And He caused His commands to ascend as a sweet savour acceptable before Him all the days….

There (were) two and twenty heads of mankind from Adam to Jacob, and two and twenty kinds of work were made until the seventh day; this is blessed and holy; and the former also is blessed and holy; and this one serves with that one for sanctification and blessing.

And to this (Jacob and his seed) it was granted that they should always be the blessed and holy ones of the first testimony and law, even as He had sanctified and blessed the Sabbath day on the seventh day.

He created heaven and earth and everything that He created in six days, and Elohim (God) made the seventh day holy, for all His works; therefore He commanded on its behalf that, whoever does any work thereon shall die, and that he who defiles it shall surely die.

Wherefore do you command the children of Yashar’el (Israel) to observe this day that they may keep it holy and not do thereon any work, and not to defile it, as it is holier than all other days. And whoever profanes it shall surely die, and whoever does thereon any work shall surely die eternally, that the children of Yashar’el (Israel) may observe this day throughout their generations, and not be rooted out of the land; for it is a holy day and a blessed day.
And every one who observes it and keeps Sabbath thereon from all his work, will be holy and blessed throughout all days like to us.

Declare and say to the children of Yashar’el (Israel) the law of this day both that they should keep Sabbath thereon, and that they should not forsake it in the error of their hearts; (and) that it is not lawful to do any work thereon which is unseemly, to do thereon their own pleasure, and that they should not prepare thereon anything to be eaten or drunk. and (that it is not lawful) to draw water, or bring in or take out thereon through their gates any burden, which they had not prepared for themselves on the sixth day in their dwellings.

And they shall not bring in nor take out from house to house on that day; for that day is more holy and blessed than any jubilee day of the jubilees: on this we kept Sabbath in the heavens before it was made known to any flesh to keep Sabbath thereon on the earth.

And the Creator of all things blessed it, but He did not sanctify all peoples and nations to keep Sabbath thereon, but Yashar’el (Israel) alone: them alone He permitted to eat and drink and to keep Sabbath thereon on the earth. And the Creator of all things blessed this day which He had created for a blessing and a sanctification and a glory above all days.
This law and testimony was given to the children of Yashar’el (Israel) as a law for ever to their generations.

chapters.commentary: Genesis 1 told from the angel’s vantage. Two and twenty kinds of work across six days, twenty-two heads of mankind from Adam to Jacob — Jubilees is making a parallel, and the parallel is structural, not decorative. The twenty-two works of creation answer to the twenty-two patriarchal heads, and the seventh day answers to the sanctified line. Creation is not raw material; it is patterned, and the pattern bends toward the sabbath at one end and toward Jacob at the other. The sabbath is the chapter’s load. Verse 17 names it as the great sign that Yahuah (God) gave to the angels of the presence and the angels of sanctification, who keep it with him in heaven and on earth. Verse 18 extends the keeping: he hides them — the angels — to keep the sabbath with him. Verse 30 names what no Christian commentary on Genesis 1 has the room to absorb: on this we kept Sabbath in the heavens before it was made known to any flesh to keep Sabbath thereon on the earth. The sabbath is older than humanity. The sabbath is older than Sinai. The sabbath is the rhythm of heaven, ratified into the creation of the earth, then disclosed to a people Yahuah (God) set apart to keep it in the world. This is the verse the horn cannot abide. Institutional Christianity moved the day under Constantine in 321 AD and ratified the move at the Council of Laodicea in 363, and has spent seventeen centuries telling the people in the pews that the sabbath was a Yahudi (Jewish) ordinance, a temporary ceremonial, a shadow that the resurrection abolished. Jubilees says otherwise on every line. The sabbath is heaven’s day. The sabbath is the Creator’s rest. The sabbath is the sign Yahuah (God) gave a peculiar people above all peoples that they should keep it together with the angels. Did God really say? The serpent has been asking this question of the seventh day from every Sunday pulpit for seventeen centuries. The answer Jubilees gives, before Sinai, before Moses, before Abraham, is: yes. He said. Verse 20 is the chapter’s other gravitational pull. I have chosen the seed of Jacob from amongst all that I have seen, and have written him down as my firstborn son, and have sanctified him to myself for ever and ever; and I will teach them the Sabbath day, that they may keep Sabbath thereon from all work. Two things to notice. First, the seed of Jacob — the covenant people, the twelve tribes through their patriarch — is named the firstborn son, and the firstborn-son language is what Yahuah (God) will speak again to Pharaoh in Exodus 4:22, and what the prophets will speak again of the gathered house. Second, the sabbath is the gift to that firstborn son. The peculiar people of verse 31 — He did not sanctify all peoples and nations to keep Sabbath thereon, but Yashar’el (Israel) alone — is not a verse to flinch at. It is the verse the inclusion gospels in every house need to flatten. The sabbath is the rest of Yahuah (God), given to the covenant body Yahuah (God) named, kept by the covenant body Yahuah (God) preserved, scattered with that covenant body when Yahuah (God) divorced Yashar’el (Israel) for breaking it — and being recovered now, in the second recovery, by the sheep coming home.
