The replacement readings — the church's spiritualization of Zion, Hebrew roots' assumption that anyone who keeps Torah inherits the mountains, Islam's transfer of the patriarchal inheritance to a different geography altogether — all require the chapter's geographical specificity to be allegorized away. The chapter resists every allegory. The chapter names the rivers. The line of Shem will narrow further as the book goes on. By chapter 11 the narrowing has reached Terah; by chapter 12 it has reached Abram; by chapter 19 it has reached Isaac; by chapter 22 it has reached Jacob; by chapter 32 it has narrowed to the priestly line through Levi while the kingly line continues through Yahudah (Judah). But the narrowing inside Shem does not negate the broader assignment to Shem. The whole Shemitic inheritance — the middle of the earth, the holy mountains, the land of the rivers — is given to Shem at chapter 8, and the elect line that will later carry the priesthood and the throne is one specific narrowing inside that broader Shemitic gift. The grandsons of Shem who do not descend into the elect line are not disinherited from the Shemitic assignment. They are simply not the line through whom the Messiah (Christ) would come. The book holds both registers at once. So should the reader.

chapters.title: The Division of the Earth

verses.text: And Ham divided amongst his sons, and the first portion came forth for Cush towards the east, and to the west of him for Mizraim, and to the west . of him for Put, and to the west of him and to the west thereof on the sea for Canaan.

And Sherri also divided amongst his sons, and the first portion came forth for Elam and his sons, to the east of the river Tigris till it approaches the east, the whole land of India, and on the Red Sea on its coast, and the waters of Dêdân, and all the mountains of Mebrî and ’Êlâ, and all the land of Sûsân and all that is on the side of Pharnâk to the Red Sea and the river Tînâ.
And for Asshur came forth the second portion, all the land of Asshur and Nineveh and Shinar and to the border of India, and it ascends and skirts the river.

And for Arpachshad came forth the third portion, all the land of the region of the Chaldees to the east of the Euphrates, bordering on the Red Sea, and all the waters of the desert close to the tongue of the sea which looks towards Egypt, all the land of Lebanon and Sanîr and ’Amânâ to the border of the Euphrates.

And for Aram there came forth the fourth portion, all the land of Mesopotamia between the Tigris and the Euphrates to the north of the Chaldees to the border of the mountains of Asshur and the land of ’Arârâ.

And there came forth for Lud the fifth portion, the mountains of Asshur and all appertaining to them till it reaches the Great Sea, and till it reaches the east of Asshur his brother. And Japheth also divided the land of his inheritance amongst his sons.

And the first portion came forth for Gomer to the east from the north side to the river Tînâ; and in the north there came forth for Magog all the inner portions of the north until it reaches to the sea of Mê’at.
And for Madai came forth as his portion that he should possess from the west of his two brothers to the islands, and to the coasts of the islands.
And for Javan came forth the fourth portion every island and the islands which are towards the border of Lud.

And for Tubal there came forth the fifth portion in the midst of the tongue which approaches towards the border of the portion of Lud to the second tongue, to the region beyond the second tongue to the third tongue.

And for Meshech came forth the sixth portion, all the region beyond the third tongue till it approaches the east of Gâdîr. And for Tiras there came forth the seventh portion, four great islands in the midst of the sea, which reach to the portion of Ham and the islands of Kamâtûrî came out by lot for the sons of Arpachshad as his inheritance.

And thus the sons of Noah divided to their sons in the presence of Noah their father, and he bound them all by an oath, imprecating a curse on every one that sought to seize the portion which had not fallen (to him) by his lot.

And they all said, “So be it; so be it,” for themselves and their sons for ever throughout their generations till the day of judgment, on which Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) shall judge them with a sword and with fire, for all the unclean wickedness of their errors, wherewith they have filled the earth with transgression and uncleanness and fornication and sin.

chapters.commentary: The subdivision among the grandchildren. Each of Shem’s, Ham’s, and Japheth’s sons receives a portion drawn by lot in the presence of Noah their father, and Noah binds them all by an oath: cursed be the one who seizes the portion that did not fall to him. And they all said, “So be it; so be it,” for themselves and their sons for ever throughout their generations till the day of judgment. Two things this chapter does for the rest of the book. First, it establishes that the boundaries of the nations are not arbitrary. They are drawn by lot in the presence of Noah, sworn to in the presence of Yahuah (God), and engraved as inheritance for their generations. This is what Deuteronomy 32:8 will later confirm: when the El Elyon (Most High) divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Yashar’el (Israel). The geography of the post-Flood world is covenantal. The displacement of peoples by violence — by the seizing of land that did not fall by lot — is a covenantal violation, and Canaan’s seizure of the land of Lebanon (chapter 10) will be exactly that. Second, the chapter prepares the reader to keep two distinctions in view simultaneously: the elect line will narrow inside Shem (Shem → Arpachshad → Eber → Peleg → Reu → Serug → Nahor → Terah → Abram), but the line of the elect remains one branch within Shem, and Shem remains one of three brothers whose nations all carry the inheritance Yahuah (God) sworn to Noah. The elect line is not ethnic-Shemitic universalism. It is a specific narrowing inside the broader assignment, and the narrowing is not the negation of the assignment. This will matter when the prophets later promise that the nations will come to your light (Isaiah 60:3) — the nations are not absorbed into Yashar’el (Israel); they remain the nations Yahuah (God) divided in chapter 9, and they come to Yashar’el’s (Israel’s) light without losing their distinction. Three categories. Not two. The covenantal architecture the chapter establishes — boundaries drawn by lot, sworn to in the presence of Yahuah (God), engraved as inheritance for the generations until the day of judgment — is the architecture Deuteronomy 32:8 reaches back for. The Masoretic text of Deuteronomy 32:8 reads according to the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and the inherited Christian and Yahudi (Jewish) commentary tradition has labored to explain how the nations of the earth could have been divided according to the number of a people not yet existing in the days of the dividing. The labor has been costly. The labor was unnecessary. The Septuagint and the Qumran witnesses to Deuteronomy 32:8 — confirmed at 4Q37, the Deuteronomy fragment from cave four — read according to the number of the sons of Elohim (God). The reading is older. The reading makes the sentence say what Jubilees 15:30–31 also says: the nations were divided to the angelic governors who were assigned over them, while Yahuah (God) kept Yashar'el (Israel) for himself, over them did He appoint no angel or spirit to lead them astray, but He alone is their ruler. The nations are under intermediate authorities. Yashar'el (Israel) is under Yahuah (God) directly. The architecture is real, and the architecture is engraved at chapter 9 of Jubilees as the lot-drawn boundaries the grandsons of Noah swore to keep. The covenantal force of the boundary-drawing has consequences the chapter sets up for the rest of the book. Land taken outside the lot is land taken in violation of the oath the patriarchs swore in the presence of Noah and Yahuah (God). Canaan's seizure of the Lebanon coast at chapter 10 is the first violation. The grandsons of Esau who push the descendants of Yahudah (Judah) out of the southern reaches at the period of the divided kingdom would be a later violation. The Babylonian and Roman seizures of the land Yahuah (God) had assigned to Yashar'el (Israel) are violations. The pattern runs through the whole biblical narrative because the architecture was established here, in the third decade of the book, and the architecture has not been repealed. The chapter also sets up what the prophets will later say about the nations coming to Yashar'el's (Israel's) light without losing their distinction. The line the nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising (Isaiah 60:3) is not an integration verse. It is a procession verse. The nations remain the nations Yahuah (God) divided in chapter 9 of Jubilees. They retain their distinct inheritance, their distinct geography, their distinct heritage. They come to Yashar'el (Israel) — to the light Yahuah (God) has caused to rise on his covenant body — and they bring their treasures and their kings and the wealth of their nations into the city of Zion as procession, as homage, as recognition. They do not become Yashar'el (Israel). They cannot become Yashar'el (Israel), because the bloodline of the twelve tribes is not a category the nations can enter by conversion. The Torah-stranger and Torah-sojourner provisions, which permit the foreigner to dwell in the land and to keep the festivals alongside the covenant body, do not transfer the foreigner's lineage. The foreigner remains a foreigner blessed inside the covenant household. The covenant body remains the twelve tribes through Jacob. This is the chapter Hebrew roots communities must read with the most care. The chapter does not say that the nations are nothing. The chapter does not say that the nations have no place at the table. The chapter says that the place at the table is not the place of the seed of promise — the nations have their own places, their own inheritances, their own assignments under the angelic governors Yahuah (God) appointed over them, and the table the Father has set in Zion welcomes them as honored guests, as friends, as the second-temple stranger and sojourner that the Torah explicitly provides for. But the table is set by the body of the seed, in the land of the seed, on the calendar Yahuah (God) gave the seed, and the seat at the head of the table belongs to Yahudah (Judah) and the throne of David. The false-inclusion gospel attempts to seat the nations at the head of the table by collapsing the distinction the chapter establishes. The chapter forecloses the collapse. The nations are honored. The nations are loved. The nations are not the seed.

chapters.title: Mastema, Babel, and the Scattering

verses.text: And in the third week of this jubilee the unclean demons began to lead astray the children of the sons of Noah; and to make to err and destroy them.
And the sons of Noah came to Noah their father, and they told him concerning the demons which were, leading astray and blinding and slaying his sons’ sons.

And he prayed before Yahuah (God) his Elohim (God), and said: Elohim (God) of the spirits of all flesh, who have shown mercy to me, And have saved me and my sons from the waters of the flood, And have not caused me to perish as You did the sons of perdition; For Your grace has been great towards me, And great has been Your mercy to my soul; Let Your grace be lift up upon my sons, And let not wicked spirits rule over them Lest they should destroy them from the earth. But do You bless me and my sons, that we may increase and multiply and replenish the earth.

And You know how Your Watchers, the fathers of these spirits, acted in my day: and as for these spirits which are living, imprison them and hold them fast in the place of condemnation, and let them not bring destruction on the sons of your servant, my Elohim (God); for these are malignant, and created in order to destroy.
And let them not rule over the spirits of the living; for You alone can exercise dominion over them. And let them not have power over the sons of the righteous from henceforth and for evermore."
And Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) bade us to bind all.

And the chief of the spirits, Mastêmâ, came and said: “Yahuah (God), Creator, let some of them remain before me, and let them hearken to my voice, and do all that I shall say to them; for if some of them are not left to me, I shall not be able to execute the power of my will on the sons of men; for these are for corruption and leading astray before my judgment, for great is the wickedness of the sons of men.” And He said: “Let the tenth part of them remain before him, and let nine parts descend into the place of condemnation.”
And one of us He commanded that we should teach Noah all their medicines; for He knew that they would not walk in uprightness, nor strive in righteousness.
And we did according to all His words: all the malignant evil ones we bound in the place of condemnation, and a tenth part of them we left that they might be subject before Satan on the earth.
And we explained to Noah all the medicines of their diseases, together with their seductions, how he might heal them with herbs of the earth.

And Noah wrote down all things in a book as we instructed him concerning every kind of medicine. Thus the evil spirits were precluded from (hurting) the sons of Noah. And he gave all that he had written to Shem, his eldest son; for he loved him exceedingly above all his sons.
And Noah slept with his fathers, and was buried on Mount Lûbâr in the land of Ararat.
Nine hundred and fifty years he completed in his life, nineteen jubilees and two weeks and five years.

And in his life on earth he excelled the children of men save Enoch because of the righteousness, wherein he was perfect. For Enoch’s office was ordained for a testimony to the generations of the world, 1 so that he should recount all the deeds of generation to generation, till the day of judgment. And in the three and thirtieth jubilee, in the first year in the second week, Peleg took to himself a wife, whose name was Lômnâ the daughter of Sînâ’ar, and she bare him a son in the fourth year of this week, and he called his name Reu; for he said: “Behold the children of men have become evil through the wicked purpose of building for themselves a city and a tower in the land of Shinar.”
For they departed from the land of Ararat eastward to Shinar; for in his days they built the city and the tower, saying, “Go to, let us ascend thereby into heaven.”

And they began to build, and in the fourth week they made brick with fire, and the bricks served them for stone, and the clay with which they cemented them together was asphalt which comes out of the sea, and out of the fountains of water in the land of Shinar.

And they built it: forty and three years were they building it; its breadth was 203 bricks, and the height (of a brick) was the third of one; its height amounted to 5433 cubits and 2 palms, and (the extent of one wall was) thirteen stades (and of the other thirty stades).

And Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) said to us: “Behold, they are one people, and (this) they begin to do, and now nothing will be withholden from them. Go to, let us go down and confound their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech, and they may be dispersed into cities and nations, and one purpose will no longer abide with them till the day of judgment.” And Yahuah (God) descended, and we descended with Him to see the city and the tower which the children of men had built.
And He confounded their language, and they no longer understood one another’s speech, and they ceased then to build the city and the tower.

For this reason the whole land of Shinar is called Babel, because Yahuah (God) did there confound all the language of the children of men, and from thence they were dispersed into their cities, each according to his language and his nation.
And Yahuah (God) sent a mighty wind against the tower and overthrew it upon the earth, and behold it was between Asshur and Babylon in the land of Shinar, and they called its name “Overthrow.”

In the fourth week in the first year in the beginning thereof in the four and thirtieth jubilee, were they dispersed from the land of Shinar. And Ham and his sons went into the land which he was to occupy, which he acquired as his portion in the land of the south.

And Canaan saw the land of Lebanon to the river of Egypt that it was very good, and he went not into the land of his inheritance to the west (that is to) the sea, and he dwelt in the land of Lebanon, eastward and westward from the border of Jordan and from the border of the sea.

And Ham, his father, and Cush and Mizraim, his brothers, said to him: “You have settled in a land which. is not your, and which did not fall to us by lot: do not do so; for if you do do so, you and your sons will fall in the land and (be) accursed through sedition; for by sedition you have settled, and by sedition will your children fall, and you shall be rooted out for ever.
Dwell not in the dwelling of Shem; for to Shem and to his sons did it come by their lot.

Cursed are you, and cursed shall you be beyond all the sons of Noah, by the curse by which we bound ourselves by an oath in the presence of the holy judge, and in the presence of Noah our father.” But he did not hearken to them, and dwelt in the land of Lebanon from Hamath to the entering of Egypt, he and his sons until this day.
And for this reason that land is named Canaan.

And Japheth and his sons went towards the sea and dwelt in the land of their portion, and Madai saw the land of the sea and it did not please him, and he begged a (portion) from Elam and Asshur and Arpachshad, his wife’s brother, and he dwelt in the land of Media, near to his wife’s brother until this day.
And he called his dwelling-place, and the dwelling-place of his sons, Media, after the name of their father Madai.

chapters.commentary: The chapter has three movements that look unrelated and are not. First, the unclean demons begin to lead astray Noah’s grandchildren (verses 1–17). Second, Babel is built and overthrown (verses 18–27). Third, Canaan seizes the land of Lebanon in defiance of his lot (verses 28–34). Three movements; one underlying claim. The post-Flood world is populated by spiritual rebellion as much as physical, and the boundaries Yahuah (God) drew in chapter 9 are violated immediately. The first movement is one of the most consequential paragraphs in Jubilees. The unclean demons — the disembodied spirits of the giants, the Watchers’ offspring drowned in the Flood — begin destroying Noah’s descendants. Noah prays. And Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) bade us to bind all. But then the chief of the spirits, Mastêmâ, came and said: “Yahuah (God), Creator, let some of them remain before me, and let them hearken to my voice, and do all that I shall say to them; for if some of them are not left to me, I shall not be able to execute the power of my will on the sons of men.” And Yahuah (God) grants the bargain: nine parts bound, one part left to Mastema’s command. This is the chapter that names the architecture every reader of the prophets and the apostles needs to keep in view. There is one Father. There is one Adversary — Mastema, also Beliar, also called Satan in verse 11 — who operates not as Yahuah (God)’s equal but as Yahuah (God)’s permitted accuser, with a tenth of the unclean spirits at his command, until the appointed end. Mastema bargains in chapter 10. Mastema afflicts Abram with the ravens in chapter 11. Mastema proposes the binding of Isaac in chapter 17. Mastema is put to shame at Moriah in chapter 18. Mastema is bound at the Passover in chapter 49. The Adversary in Jubilees is not freelance. He has a leash, and the leash is held by the Creator. This is the same architecture Job 1, Zechariah 3, and Revelation 12 will all witness to: the accuser stands before the throne, but he stands before it. Verse 12 names a small kindness that will matter. And we explained to Noah all the medicines of their diseases, together with their seductions, how he might heal them with herbs of the earth. The angels teach Noah the medicines that counter the demons’ afflictions, and Noah writes them down for Shem. The earth is not abandoned to the spirits. The Father provides. There is a healing tradition that descends through the line of the altar, alongside the priestly tradition. The covenant people are not given only a sanctuary. They are given an arsenal. The second movement is Babel. Yahuah (God) descends with the angels and confounds the speech, and the chapter is at pains to specify the mechanism: one purpose will no longer abide with them till the day of judgment (verse 22). The scattering at Babel is not an arbitrary punishment. It is a containment. The men were unified around a single project — let us ascend thereby into heaven — and the unity of a fallen race in a single project is what Yahuah (God) will not permit on the earth. The scattering is mercy as much as judgment. The day of judgment will close the containment; until then, the languages keep the rebellion fragmented. The third movement is Canaan. Canaan looks at Lebanon, sees that it is good, and refuses to walk to the portion that fell to him by lot west to the sea. His father Ham, his brothers Cush and Mizraim, plead with him. You have settled in a land which is not yours, and which did not fall to us by lot. He does not hear. Cursed are you, and cursed shall you be beyond all the sons of Noah, by the curse by which we bound ourselves by an oath. The land Yashar’el (Israel) will later enter under Joshua is the land Canaan stole. The dispossession of the Canaanites under Joshua is not an arbitrary land grab; it is the covenantal undoing of Canaan’s seizure. The land returns to Shem’s inheritance, which had included it from chapter 8. The reader who has been catechized to feel guilt about the Conquest because the modern imperial mind reads the Conquest as colonial expansion is reading the wrong category onto the text. Read chapter 10 first. Then read Joshua.

chapters.title: From Reu to Abram

verses.text: And in the thirty-fifth jubilee, in the third week, in the first year thereof, Reu took to himself a wife, and her name was ’Ôrâ, the daughter of ’Ûr, the son of Kêsêd, and she bare him a son, and he called his name Sêrôḫ, in the seventh year of this week in this jubilee.

And the sons of Noah began to war on each other, to take captive and to slay each other, and to shed the blood of men on the earth, and to eat blood, and to build strong cities, and walls, and towers, and individuals (began) to exalt themselves above the nation, and to found the beginnings of kingdoms, and to go to war people against people, and nation against nation, and city against city, and all (began) to do evil, and to acquire arms, and to teach their sons war, and they began to capture cities, and to sell male and female slaves.
And ’Ûr, the son of Kêsêd, built the city of ’Arâ of the Chaldees, and called its name after his own name and the name of his father.

And they made for themselves molten images, and they worshipped each the idol, the molten image which they had made for themselves, and they began to make graven images and unclean simulacra, and malignant spirits assisted and seduced (them) into committing transgression and uncleanness.

And the prince Mastêmâ exerted himself to do all this, and he sent forth other spirits, those which were put under his hand, to do all manner of wrong and sin, and all manner of transgression, to corrupt and destroy, and to shed blood upon the earth.

For this reason he called the name of Sêrôḫ, Serug, for every one turned to do all manner of sin and transgression. And he grew up, and dwelt in Ur of the Chaldees, near to the father of his wife’s mother, and he worshipped idols, and he took to himself a wife in the thirty-sixth jubilee, in the fifth week, in the first year thereof, and her name was Mêlkâ, the daughter of Kâbêr, the daughter of his father’s brother.

And she bare him Nahor, in the first year of this week, and he grew and dwelt in Ur of the Chaldees, and his father taught him the researches of the Chaldees to divine and augur, according to the signs of heaven.
And in the thirty-seventh jubilee, in the sixth week, in the first 1800 A M. year thereof, he took to himself a wife, and her name was ’Îjâskâ, the daughter of Nêstâg of the Chaldees.
And she bare him Terah in the seventh year of this week.

And the prince Mastêmâ sent ravens and birds to devour the seed which was sown in the land, in order to destroy the land, and rob the children of men of their labours. Before they could plough in the seed, the ravens picked (it) from the surface of the ground.
And for this reason he called his name Terah, because the ravens and the birds reduced them to destitution and devoured their seed.

And the years began to be barren, owing to the birds, and they devoured all the fruit of the trees from the trees: it was only with great effort that they could save a little of all the fruit of the earth in their days.

And in this thirty-ninth jubilee, in the second week in the first year, Terah took to himself a wife, and her name was ’Êdnâ, the daughter of ’Abrâm the daughter of his father’s sister. And in the seventh year of this week she bare him a son, and he called his name Abram, by the name of the father of his mother; for he had died before his daughter had conceived a son. And the child began to understand the errors of the earth that all went astray after graven images and after uncleanness, and his father taught him writing, and he was two weeks of years old, and he separated himself from his father that he might not worship idols with him.
And he began to pray to the Creator of all things that He might save him from the errors of the children of men, and that his portion should not fall into error after uncleanness and vileness.

And the seed time came for the sowing of seed upon the land, and they all went forth together to protect their seed against the ravens, and Abram went forth with those that went, and the child was a lad of fourteen years.

And a cloud of ravens came to devour the seed, and Abram ran to meet them before they settled on the ground, and cried to them before they settled on the ground to devour the seed, and said, “Descend not: return to the place whence you came,” and they proceeded to turn back.

And he caused the clouds of ravens to turn back that day seventy times, and of all the ravens throughout all the land where Abram was there settled there not so much as one. And all who were with him throughout all the land saw him cry out, and all the ravens turn back, and his name became great in all the land of the Chaldees.

And there came to him this year all those that wished to sow, and he went with them until the time of sowing ceased: and they sowed their land, and that year they brought enough grain home and ate and were satisfied.

And in the first year of the fifth week Abram taught those who made implements for oxen, the artificers in wood, and they made a vessel above the ground, facing the frame of the plough, in order to put the seed thereon, and the seed fell down therefrom upon the share of the plough, and was hidden in the earth, and they no longer feared the ravens.

And after this manner they made (vessels) above the ground on all the frames of the ploughs, and they sowed and tilled all the land, according as Abram commanded them, and they no longer feared the birds.

chapters.commentary: The line continues to narrow, and the world continues to rot. The sons of Noah began to war on each other, to take captive and to slay each other, and to shed the blood of men on the earth, and to eat blood, and to build strong cities, and walls, and towers, and individuals (began) to exalt themselves above the nation, and to found the beginnings of kingdoms. Three things to register here. First, kingship is not in the original design. Yahuah (God) gave Noah’s sons portions, not crowns. The first kingdoms in Jubilees are the consequence of post-Babel fragmentation, where men exalted themselves above the nation. By the time Yashar’el (Israel) asks for a king in 1 Samuel 8, the request is the late echo of an old corruption. Second, the eating of blood has returned — the sons of Noah have undone Noah’s covenant — which is why chapter 6 had to ordain the prohibition again at Sinai. The world Noah left behind did not stay clean. Third, they made for themselves molten images, and they worshipped each the idol (verse 4). Idolatry does not need a long time to take root. By Reu’s generation it is everywhere. Verse 5 names the engine. And the prince Mastêmâ exerted himself to do all this, and he sent forth other spirits, those which were put under his hand, to do all manner of wrong and sin, and all manner of transgression, to corrupt and destroy, and to shed blood upon the earth. The bargain Mastema struck in chapter 10 is now operative. The tenth of the demonic forces left to him is at work. The reader who came up in modern Christianity, where personal evil and demonic agency are often dismissed as superstition, has to readjust the lens here. Jubilees does not separate moral evil from spiritual influence. The two are partners. The corruption of the post-Flood world is not self-generating. It is animated. The chapter then narrows. Reu, Serug, Nahor, Terah, and finally Abram. Abram is born into Ur of the Chaldees, and his father Terah teaches his son Nahor the researches of the Chaldees to divine and augur, according to the signs of heaven (verse 8). The omen-craft Kâinâm copied from the Watchers’ rock in chapter 8 has become the family trade. Abram is born into a household practicing the spiritual fraud that traces directly back to the Watchers, in a culture sliding into idolatry, in a city named after Mastema’s instrument. The seed of promise enters the most contaminated household in the chapter on purpose. The narrowing of the elect line is not the rescue of the already-clean. It is the call out of the dirty. Verse 11 records Mastema’s harassment of the agricultural cycle — Mastêmâ sent ravens and birds to devour the seed which was sown in the land. Famine, locust, and the swarm of birds that destroy the sowing are not always weather. Sometimes they are the Adversary at work, with permission. The years began to be barren. Terah is named Terah — because the ravens and the birds reduced them to destitution and devoured their seed. Then the chapter pivots to Abram at fourteen years old. The child began to understand the errors of the earth that all went astray after graven images and after uncleanness, and his father taught him writing, and he was two weeks of years old, and he separated himself from his father that he might not worship idols with him. Notice the order. Abram first separates himself. Abram first prays to the Creator to save him from the errors. Abram first acts on the truth he has been given by something other than his father. Then the call comes in chapter 12. The call of Abram does not begin with a voice from heaven. It begins with a fourteen-year-old refusing his father’s idols. The chapter ends with Abram driving the ravens off the seed. The fields are saved. The same harassment Mastema authored against the land is undone by the prayer of the boy. Verse 22: they sowed their land, and that year they brought enough grain home and ate and were satisfied. The kingdom of the Adversary is permitted, but it is not final. The simple prayer of an obedient boy, on the open field, broke its grip on a year’s harvest. This is what awakening looks like at ground level. It does not begin with a movement. It begins with one person who refuses the lie and prays.

chapters.title: Abram Burns the Idols

verses.text: And it came to pass in the sixth week, in the seventh year thereof, that Abram said to Terah his father, saying, “Father!” And he said, “Behold, here am I, my son.”

And he said, "What help and profit have we from those idols which you do worship, And before which you do bow yourself? For there is no spirit in them, For they are dumb forms, and a misleading of the heart. Worship them not: Worship the Elohim (God) of heaven, Who causes the rain and the dew to descend on the earth, And does everything upon the earth, And has created everything by His word, And all life is from before His face. Why do you worship things that have no spirit in them? For they are the work of (men’s) hands, And on your shoulders do you bear them, And you have no help from them, But they are a great cause of shame to those who make them, And a misleading of the heart to those who worship them: Worship them not." And his father said to him, “I also know it, my son, but what shall I do with a people who have made me to serve before them?
And if I tell them the truth, they will slay me; for their soul cleaves to them to worship them and honour them. Keep silent, my son, lest they slay you.”
And these words he spake to his two brothers, and they were angry with him and he kept silent.
And in the fortieth jubilee, in the second week, in the seventh year thereof, Abram took to himself a wife, and her name was Sarai, the daughter of his father, and she became his wife.

And Haran, his brother, took to himself a wife in the third year of the third week, and she bare him a son in the seventh year of this week and he called his name Lot. And Nahor, his brother, took to himself a wife.

And in the sixtieth year of the life of Abram, that is, in the fourth week, in the fourth year thereof, Abram arose by night, and burned the house of the idols, and he burned all that was in the house, and no man knew it.
And they arose in the night and sought to save their gods from the midst of the fire.

And Haran hasted to save them, but the fire flamed over him, and he was burnt in the fire, and he died in Ur of the Chaldees before Terah his father, and they buried him in Ur of the Chaldees. And Terah went forth from Ur of the Chaldees, he and his sons, to go into the land of Lebanon and into the land of Canaan, and he dwelt in the land of Haran, and Abram, dwelt with Terah his father in Haran two weeks of years.

And in the sixth week, in the fifth year thereof, Abram sat up throughout the night on the new moon of the seventh month to observe the stars from the evening to the morning, in order to see what would be the character of the year with regard to the rains, and he was alone as he sat and observed.

And a word came into his heart and he said: "All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun are all in the hand of Yahuah (God). Why do I search (them) out? If He desires, He causes it to rain, morning and evening; And if He desires, He withholds it, And all things are in His hand." And he prayed that night and said "My Elohim (God), Elohim (God) El Elyon (Most High), You alone are my Elohim (God), And You and Your dominion have I chosen. And You have created all things, And all things that are are the work of Your hands. Deliver me from the hands of evil spirits who have sway over the thoughts of men’s hearts, And let them not lead me astray from You, my Elohim (God). And stablish You me and my seed for ever That we go not astray from henceforth and for evermore." And he said Shall I return to Ur of the Chaldees who seek my face that I may return to them, or am I to remain here in this place? The right path before You prosper it in the hands of Your servant that he may fulfil (it) and that I may not walk in the deceitfulness of my heart, O my Elohim (God)."

And he made an end of speaking and praying, and behold the word of Yahuah (God) was sent to him through me, saying: "Get you up from your country, and from your kindred and from the house of your father to a land which I shall show you, and I shall make you a great and numerous nation. And I shall bless you And I shall make your name great, And you will be blessed in the earth, And in you will all families of the earth be blessed, And I shall bless them that bless you, And curse them that curse you. And I shall be a Elohim (God) to you and your son, and to your son’s son, and to all your seed: fear not, from henceforth and to all generations of the earth I am your Elohim (God)."

And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) said: “Open his mouth and his ears, that he may hear and speak with his mouth, with the language which has been revealed”; for it had ceased from the mouths of all the children of men from the day of the overthrow (of Babel).
And I opened his mouth, and his ears and his lips, and I began to speak with him in Hebrew in the tongue of the creation.

And he took the books of his fathers, and these were written in Hebrew and he transcribed them, and he began from henceforth to study them, and I made known to him that which he could not (understand), and he studied them during the six rainy months.

And it came to pass in the seventh year of the sixth week that he spoke to his father, and informed him that he would leave Haran to go into the land of Canaan to see it and return to him. And Terah his father said to him; "Go in peace: May the eternal Elohim (God) make your path straight, And Yahuah (God) (be) with you, and protect you from all evil, And grant to you grace, mercy and favour before those who see you, And may none of the children of men have power over you to harm you; Go in peace. And if you see a land pleasant to your eyes to dwell in, then arise and take me to you and take Lot with you, the son of Haran your brother, as your own son: Yahuah (God) be with you.
And Nahor your brother leave with me till you return in peace, and we go with you all together."

chapters.commentary: The chapter opens with Abram’s confrontation of Terah. What help and profit have we from those idols which you do worship, and before which you do bow yourself? For there is no spirit in them, for they are dumb forms, and a misleading of the heart. Terah’s reply is the chapter’s quiet horror: I also know it, my son, but what shall I do with a people who have made me to serve before them? And if I tell them the truth, they will slay me; for their soul cleaves to them to worship them and honour them. Keep silent, my son, lest they slay you. Three categories of person sit in the chapter so far. The wholly deceived (the city). The captive functionary who knows the truth and serves the lie because telling the truth costs his life (Terah). The awakened son who will not stay in either category (Abram). The middle category is the one to have patience for. Terah is not the enemy of the chapter. Terah is the captive functionary, the man who knows better and is afraid to speak. He is the chaplain in the false system, the pastor in the four-house pulpit who preaches what he does not fully believe because the people will not hear what he does. The way out of his position is not condemnation. The way out is for the son to act. The pulpit functionary often comes home behind the awakened son, in the years after, when he sees his son survive what he was afraid to say. Abram acts. Abram arose by night, and burned the house of the idols, and he burned all that was in the house, and no man knew it. The chapter notes that Haran rushed in to save the gods and was burned in the fire. The lesson is plain: the idols cannot save the man who defends them. The man who runs into the burning house to rescue what his hand made dies with what his hand made. Haran perishes in Ur of the Chaldees, and Terah at last leaves the city, taking Abram and the family with him. Verses 16–22 record Abram’s first night of star-watching in Haran — sitting up to read the rains in the heavens, the way he had been trained by his fathers. And the word comes into his heart and breaks the chain. All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun are all in the hand of Yahuah (God). Why do I search them out? The Watchers’ inheritance lifts off him in one sentence. He prays the prayer that converts the rest of his life: My Elohim (God), Elohim (God) El Elyon (Most High), You alone are my Elohim (God), and You and Your dominion have I chosen. And the call comes. Get you up from your country, and from your kindred and from the house of your father to a land which I shall show you. The chapter’s last gift: verse 25 names the recovery of the original language. Yahuah (God) sends the angel of the presence to open Abram’s mouth, and the angel says, I began to speak with him in Hebrew in the tongue of the creation. And he took the books of his fathers, and these were written in Hebrew and he transcribed them, and he began from henceforth to study them, and I made known to him that which he could not (understand), and he studied them during the six rainy months. The books of the fathers — Adam’s, Enoch’s, Noah’s — written in the language of creation, lost since Babel, restored to Abram on the night his call comes. Abram does not start the covenant from zero. He recovers the deposit his fathers had carried before the scattering. The covenant the prophets will later promise to gather into one is not a new thing. It is the restoration of an old thing the city of his birth had buried.

chapters.title: Abram, Lot, and the Land

verses.text: And Abram journeyed from Haran, and he took Sarai, his wife, and Lot his brother Haran’s son, to the land of Canaan, and he came into Asshur, and proceeded to Shechem, and dwelt near a lofty oak.
And he saw, and, behold, the land was very pleasant from the entering of Hamath to the lofty oak. . And Yahuah (God) said to him: “To you and to your seed will I give this land.”
And he built an altar there, and he offered thereon a burnt sacrifice to Yahuah (God), who had appeared to him.
And he removed from thence to the mountain… 3 Bethel on the west and Ai on the east, and pitched his tent there.

And he saw and behold, the land was very wide and good, and everything grew thereon–vines and figs and pomegranates, oaks and ilexes, and terebinths and oil trees, and cedars and cypresses and date trees, and all trees of the field, and there was water on the mountains.

And he blessed Yahuah (God) who had led him out of Ur of the Chaldees, and had brought him to this land. And it came to pass in the first year, in the seventh week, on the new moon of the first month, that he built an altar on this mountain, and called on the name of Yahuah (God): “You, the eternal Elohim (God), are my Elohim (God).”
And he offered on the altar a burnt sacrifice to Yahuah (God) that He should be with him and not forsake him all the days of his life.

And he removed from thence and went towards the south, and he came to Hebron, and Hebron was built at, that time, and he dwelt there two years, and he went (thence) into the land of the south, to Bealoth and there was a famine in the land.
And Abram went into Egypt in the third year of the week, and he dwelt in Egypt five years before his wife was torn away from him.

NOW Tanais in Egypt was at that time built–seven years after Hebron. 11 And it came to pass when Pharaoh seized Sarai, the wife of Abram, that Yahuah (God) plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.

And Abram was very glorious by reason of possessions in sheep, and cattle, and asses, and horses, and camels, and menservants, and maidservants, and in silver and gold exceedingly. And Lot also, his brother’s son, was wealthy.

And Pharaoh gave back Sarai, the wife of Abram, and he sent him out of the land of Egypt, and he journeyed to the place where he had pitched his tent at the beginning, to the place of the altar, with Ai on the east, and Bethel on the west, and he blessed Yahuah (God) his Elohim (God) who had brought him back in peace. And it came to pass in the forty-first jubilee, in the third year of the first week, that he returned to this place and offered thereon a burnt sacrifice, and called on the name of Yahuah (God), and said: “You, the most high Elohim (God), are my Elohim (God) for ever and ever.”
And in the fourth year of this week Lot parted from him, and Lot dwelt in Sodom, and the men of Sodom were sinners exceedingly.
And it grieved him in his heart that his brother’s son had parted from him; for he had no children.

In that year when Lot was taken captive, Yahuah (God) said to Abram, after that Lot had parted from him, in the fourth year of this week: "Lift up your eyes from the place where you are dwelling, northward and southward, and westward and eastward.

For all the land which you see I shall give to you and to your seed for ever, and I shall make your seed as the sand of the sea: though a man may number the dust of the earth, yet your seed shall not be numbered. Arise, walk (through the land) in the length of it and the breadth of it, and see it all; for to your seed shall I give it." And Abram went to Hebron, and dwelt there. And in this year came Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, and Amraphel, king of Shinar, and Arioch, king of Sêllâsar and Têrgâl, king of nations, and slew the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Sodom fled, and many fell through wounds in the vale of Siddim, by the Salt Sea.
And they took captive Sodom and Adam and Zeboim, and they took captive Lot also, the son of Abram’s brother, and all his possessions, and they went to Dan.

And one who had escaped came and told Abram that his brother’s son had been taken captive and (Abram) armed his household servants. 25…………. for Abram, and for his seed, a tenth of the first-fruits to Yahuah (God), and Yahuah (God) ordained it as an ordinance for ever that they should give it to the priests who served before Him, that they should possess it for ever.

And to this law there is no limit of days; for He has ordained it for the generations for ever that they should give to Yahuah (God) the tenth of everything, of the seed and of the wine and of the oil and of the cattle and of the sheep.

And He gave (it) to His priests to eat and to drink with joy before Him. And the king of Sodom came to him and bowed himself before him, and said: “Our Yahuah (God) Abram, give to us the souls which you have rescued, but let the booty be your.”

And Abram said to him: “I lift up my hands to the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), that from a thread to a shoe-latchet I shall not take aught that is your, lest you should say I have made Abram rich; save only what the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me–Aner, Eschol, and Mamre. These will take their portion.”

chapters.commentary: Abram journeys to Canaan. He builds altars at Shechem (the lofty oak), between Bethel and Ai, and at Hebron. The chapter is patient with the geography because the geography is the inheritance. He is being walked through the land Yahuah (God) will give to his seed, and at each stop he builds an altar and calls on the name of Yahuah (God). Verse 8: he built an altar on this mountain, and called on the name of Yahuah (God): “You, the eternal Elohim (God), are my Elohim (God).” This is what worship looks like in the chapter: an altar, a name, a confession of personal allegiance. There is no city, no temple, no priesthood yet. There is a man who has been called and the Father he has chosen. The famine sends Abram to Egypt, and the chapter handles the Sarai episode in fewer verses than Genesis. Pharaoh seizes her; Yahuah (God) plagues Pharaoh; Pharaoh returns her; Abram leaves Egypt enriched, returns to the altar between Bethel and Ai, and blesses Yahuah (God). The episode is held lightly because Jubilees is in a hurry to get to the separation from Lot, which the chapter weights heavily. Lot parts from Abram and dwells in Sodom (verse 17). And the men of Sodom were sinners exceedingly. And it grieved him in his heart that his brother’s son had parted from him; for he had no children. Jubilees registers Abram’s grief specifically because the grief is the chapter’s emotional engine. Lot was the closest thing to a son Abram had. The narrative of the elect line is also the narrative of the elect line’s loneliness. Abram is alone after Lot leaves. And in that loneliness, in that fourth year of the week, Yahuah (God) speaks to him after that Lot had parted from him and gives the seed promise: all the land which you see I shall give to you and to your seed for ever, and I shall make your seed as the sand of the sea. The promise comes after the loss. The promise comes to the man with no son. The chapter closes with the rescue of Lot from Chedorlaomer’s campaign and Abram’s tithe of the first-fruits to the priest of the El Elyon (Most High). Jubilees does not name Melchizedek here (the text in verse 25 has a textual gap), but the substance is the same: the tithe of the first-fruits is given to a priest who serves before Yahuah (God), and Yahuah (God) ordained it as an ordinance for ever that they should give it to the priests who served before Him. The tithe is older than Levi. The priesthood that receives it is older than Aaron. The chapter is repeating the move it made in chapter 6: the institutions of Sinai are not Sinai-novel. They are the re-disclosure of patterns engraved earlier and held by men outside the genealogy who carried what the genealogy was about to inherit. The altar Abram builds at each stop is the chapter's quietest argument. There is no priest standing at any of these altars besides Abram himself. There is no temple. There is no codified order of sacrifice. There is a man with a covenant and a fire and the name of Yahuah (God) on his tongue. The pattern is the patriarchal-priestly pattern that runs from Adam in chapter 3 through Enoch in chapter 4 through Noah in chapter 6 through Abram here at chapter 13 — every patriarch builds altars, every patriarch makes sacrifice, every patriarch calls upon the name. The Aaronic priesthood that will be installed at Sinai is not the beginning of the priesthood of Yahuah (God). The Aaronic priesthood is one specific narrowing of the priestly office for one specific period of the covenant body's life, instituted to handle the full sacrificial system at the tabernacle and later the temple. Before Aaron, the household head was the priest of his household. Before Levi, the firstborn was the priest of his line. After the temple's destruction in 70 CE, when the Aaronic priesthood was again rendered inoperative because the place of the altar was taken away, the office did not vanish. The office returned to the household. The household head became, again, the priest of his household. This is the pattern the awakening reader is recovering — not a clergy class, but the household altar Abram built between Bethel and Ai with no one but his wife and his nephew watching. The famine that drives Abram to Egypt is the chapter's first descent into Egypt, and the chapter handles it briefly because the larger descent is coming with Jacob's family at chapter 44. But the briefer descent prefigures the larger one, and the larger one prefigures the long captivity, and the long captivity prefigures every exile the body of the seed will later endure, including the present long exile of the scattered tribes among the nations of the present world. The pattern is constant. The seed of promise descends into a foreign land, is preserved there, is plundered there, is brought out by the hand of Yahuah (God) who plagues the foreign king and enriches the seed at the foreign king's expense. The Exodus pattern is older than the Exodus. Abram comes out of Egypt enriched. Jacob comes out of Padan-aram enriched. The body of Yashar'el (Israel) comes out of Egypt enriched four hundred and thirty years later. The scattered seed coming home in the present generation will, in the appointed time, also come out of the long exile not impoverished but enriched. The pattern holds because the architecture is the same architecture every time. The tithe to the priest of El Elyon (Most High) at the chapter's end is the third pre-Sinai institution Jubilees plants in the patriarchal soil before Moses. The Sabbath was hallowed at chapter 2. The festivals were kept by Noah at chapter 6. The tithe is given here at chapter 13 to a priest who serves before Yahuah (God), and the chapter notes that Yahuah (God) ordained it as an ordinance for ever that they should give it to the priests who served before Him. The priesthood that receives the tithe is not Levitical. The Levitical priesthood is four generations away. The priest who receives Abram's tithe is the priest of the El Elyon (Most High) — Melchizedek, in Genesis 14, in the parallel narrative — and the priesthood Melchizedek represents is the priesthood Hebrews 7 will later argue carries forward through the order of Yahusha (Jesus) the Messiah (Christ) himself. Jubilees does not name Melchizedek in the chapter's surviving text (the manuscript has a gap at verse 25), but the substance is unambiguous. The tithe is older than Levi. The priesthood that receives it is older than Aaron. The order of Melchizedek runs underneath the Aaronic order the entire time the Aaronic order is operative, and resumes its visibility when the Aaronic order's place of altar is taken away. The household priest who receives the tithe of his own income, the assembly elder who serves at the household altar, the body of believers gathered around the bread and the wine on the seventh day — all of these stand in the order Melchizedek occupied at chapter 13 of Jubilees, four hundred years before Aaron was born.

chapters.title: The Covenant with Abram

verses.text: After these things, in the fourth year of this week, on the new moon of the third month, the word of Yahuah (God) came to Abram in a dream, saying: “Fear not, Abram; I am your defender, and your reward will be exceeding great.”

And he said: “Yahuah (God), Yahuah (God), what will you give me, seeing I go hence childless, and the son of Mâsêq, the son of my handmaid, is the Dammasek Eliezer: he will be my heir, and to me you have given no seed.”
And He said to him: “This (man) will not be your heir, but one that will come out of your own bowels; he will be your heir.”
And He brought him forth abroad, and said to him: “Look toward heaven and number the stars, if you are able to number them.”
And he looked toward heaven, and beheld the stars. And He said to him: “So shall your seed be.”

And he believed in Yahuah (God), and it was counted to him for righteousness. And He said to him: “I am Yahuah (God) that brought you out of Ur of the Chaldees, to give you the land of the Canaanites to possess it for ever; and I shall be Elohim (God) to you and to your seed after you.”
And he said: “Yahuah (God), Yahuah (God), whereby shall I know that I shall inherit (it)?”
And he said to him: “Take Me an heifer of three years, and a goat of three years, and a sheep of three years, and a turtle-dove, and a pigeon.”
And he took all these in the middle of the month; and he dwelt at the oak of Mamre, which is near Hebron.

And he built there an altar, and sacrificed all these; and he poured their blood upon the altar, and divided them in the midst, and laid them over against each other; but the birds divided he not. And birds came down upon the pieces, and Abram drove them away, and did not suffer the birds to touch them.

And it came to pass, when the sun had set, that an ecstasy fell upon Abram, and lo! an horror of great darkness fell upon him, and it was said to Abram: “Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land (that is) not theirs, and they will bring them into bondage, and afflict them four hundred years.
And the nation also to whom they will be in bondage shall I judge, and after that they will come forth thence with much substance.
And you will go to your fathers in peace, and be buried in a good old age.

But in the fourth generation they will return hither; for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.” And he awoke from his sleep, and he arose, and the sun had set; and there was a flame, and behold! a furnace was smoking, and a flame of fire passed between the pieces.

And on that day Yahuah (God) made a covenant with Abram, saying: “To your seed will I give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates, the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites, the Perizzites, and the Rephaim, the Phakorites, and the Hivites, and the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.”
And the day passed, and Abram offered the pieces, and the birds, and their fruit-offerings, and their drink-offerings, and the fire devoured them.

And on that day we made a covenant with Abram, according as we had covenanted with Noah in this month; and Abram renewed the festival and ordinance for himself for ever. And Abram rejoiced, and made all these things known to Sarai his wife; and he believed that he would have seed, but she did not bear.
And Sarai advised her husband Abram, and said to him: “Go in to Hagar, my Egyptian maid: it may be that I shall build up seed to you by her.”
And Abram hearkened to the voice of Sarai his wife, and said to her, “Do (so).” And Sarai took Hagar, her maid, the Egyptian, and gave her to Abram, her husband, to be his wife.
And he went in to her, and she conceived and bare him a son, and he called his name Ishmael, in the fifth year of this week; and this was the eighty-sixth year in the life of Abram.

chapters.commentary: This is the chapter every reading of Paul’s letters has to pass through, and this is the chapter the inherited Christian commentary tradition has the hardest time with because Jubilees will not let the commentary tradition have what it wants. The chapter opens with Yahuah (God) coming to Abram in a dream — fear not, Abram; I am your defender, and your reward will be exceeding great — and Abram’s complaint that he has no seed. Yahuah (God) brings him outside, shows him the stars, tells him so shall your seed be, and then verse 6 records the line on which the entire Pauline argument of Romans 4 and Galatians 3 rests: And he believed in Yahuah (God), and it was counted to him for righteousness. Notice when this verse arrives in the chapter. It arrives before the covenant of the pieces (verses 9–20). It arrives long before the circumcision of chapter 15. The order Jubilees preserves is the order Paul will later make load-bearing. Abram is reckoned righteous by faith in the promise, before the covenant ritual is performed and before the sign of the covenant is given in his flesh. This sequence is not a Pauline construction. The sequence is in the text Paul read. Jubilees preserves it without commentary, and the reader who comes to it expecting either a Christian antinomian reading or a Hebrew-roots flesh-credential reading is met by the text itself: the man believed and it was counted to him for righteousness, and then the covenant was cut, and then the sign was given. The Reformation collapsed two questions into one — how is a man justified and how does a justified man live — and chose faith alone as the answer to both, producing the antinomian gospel that has spent five centuries assuring readers that the Torah was the curse the Messiah (Christ) redeemed them from. The Judaizers in Paul’s day collapsed the same two questions and chose works of the law — meaning their flesh-credential system — as the answer to both, producing the become a Yahudi (Jew) to be saved gospel Paul wrote Galatians to dismantle. Jubilees 14 does neither. The chapter holds the two questions apart by holding the sequence apart. Verse 6: faith counted for righteousness. Verses 9–20: covenant ritual. Then the covenant life that follows. Justification, then covenant cut, then covenant living. Three movements. Held distinct. Verse 16 — the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full — names a moral physics the modern reader needs to register. The Amorites’ displacement at the Conquest is not arbitrary. It has been waited out. Yahuah (God) does not displace a people whose iniquity is not yet full. Four hundred years of patience precede the judgment that comes through Joshua. The reader who has been catechized to feel that Yahuah (God) is impulsively wrathful in the Old Testament is reading the wrong category onto the text. The Old Testament Yahuah (God) waits centuries before judgment. The same waiting is what the prophets describe again when they speak of Yahuah (God)’s patience with Yashar’el (Israel) before the exile. The same waiting is what Peter will describe in 2 Peter 3 as the Father’s longsuffering toward the present world. Verses 18–20 close the chapter with the covenant cut in fire. The furnace passes between the pieces, and Abram offers the festival — verse 20: we made a covenant with Abram, according as we had covenanted with Noah in this month; and Abram renewed the festival and ordinance for himself for ever. The Feast of Weeks (chapter 6) is the month the covenant is cut. The festival keeps the covenant alive. The festival the church abolished as a Yahudi (Jewish) holiday is the festival the covenant Abram entered was sealed inside. The brief addendum on Hagar and Ishmael (verses 21–24) is the chapter acknowledging what Sarai’s impatience produced. The chapter does not moralize. It records. The seed of promise is not yet born; the seed of the maidservant is born in the meantime; the chapters that follow will have to sort out what each carries. The fire-furnace theophany at verses 18–20 is the chapter's most arresting image, and the chapter holds it without explanation because the image speaks. The pieces of the sacrifice are laid in two rows. The sun goes down. A horror of great darkness falls on Abram. And then a smoking furnace and a burning lamp pass between the pieces. The Genesis 15 parallel uses the same imagery. What walks between the pieces is what swears the oath. In the ancient near-eastern covenant ritual, the parties cut the sacrificed animals in two and walked between the pieces together, swearing in effect may this be done to me if I break this covenant. But in this covenant, only one party walks between the pieces. Abram does not walk. Abram lies in the trance. The smoking furnace and the burning lamp — Yahuah (God) himself, present in the two emblems of his presence on Sinai and in the wilderness sanctuary — walks the path of the covenant alone. The covenant is unilateral. Yahuah (God) swears it on his own name. The fulfillment does not depend on Abram's continuing performance, because Abram is not the party who walked the path. This is the chapter Paul will later read when he writes Galatians 3:17 — the covenant, that was confirmed before of Elohim (God) in the Messiah (Christ), the Torah, which was four hundred and thirty years after, cannot disannul, that it should make the promise of none effect. The covenant of the pieces is the unbreakable covenant. The Torah comes later as the covenant body's invited response to the gift, not as the gift's purchase price. The line about the Amorites in verse 16 deserves a longer dwell than the chapter's brevity allows. In the fourth generation they shall return here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full to be completed. The Amorites are not displaced for being Amorites. The Amorites are displaced for the accumulated covenant-breaking the chapter does not enumerate but the rest of the Torah will later be explicit about — the burning of children to Molech, the ritualized fertility cults that incorporated incest and bestiality and bloodshed into temple worship, the accumulated cruelty of cult-systems Yahuah (God) had warned the Amorites away from since Noah. Four generations of warning are given. Four generations of patience are extended. The displacement is the judgment of accumulated debt, not the impulsive cruelty of a tribal deity. The reader who has been catechized to find the Old Testament Yahuah (God) embarrassing is reading the wrong category onto the text. Yahuah (God) waits. Yahuah (God) waits longer than the modern reader's patience would. Yahuah (God) waits until the cup is full, and then the cup is poured out — sometimes on the Amorites, sometimes on Yashar'el (Israel) at the Babylonian exile, sometimes on the Roman empire, sometimes on the body of the present horn at the appointed time still ahead. The mechanism does not change. The Father is patient until the patience would itself become injustice. Then the verdict falls. The Feast of Weeks ratification at verse 20 — we made a covenant with Abram, according as we had covenanted with Noah in this month; and Abram renewed the festival and ordinance for himself for ever — places the entire covenant of the pieces inside the same festival window Yahuah (God) cut the rainbow covenant with Noah at chapter 6. The festivals are not occasion-markers Yahuah (God) chose at random. The festivals are the calendrical hinges on which the covenants are cut, and the covenants are cut on the festivals because the festivals were the appointed times engraved on the heavenly tables before any earthly covenant was made. The Feast of Weeks is the covenant-cutting feast. Noah's covenant was cut at it. Abram's covenant was cut at it. The Torah at Sinai was given at it (the rabbinic tradition's reading of Exodus 19's chronology lands the giving of the Torah on the same date Pentecost would later mark). The Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) was poured out at it (Acts 2 explicitly lands at the day of Pentecost, which is the Greek for the Feast of Weeks). The Father has been cutting his great covenants on this single festival from Noah forward, and the Christian relocation of Pentecost as a vague Spirit-anniversary disconnected from the Feast of Weeks calendar is one more layer of the calendar drift the angel of the presence warned Moses about at chapter 6.

chapters.title: Circumcision and the Promise

verses.text: And in the fifth year of the fourth week of this jubilee, in the third month, in the middle of the month, Abram celebrated the feast of the first-fruits of the grain harvest.

And he offered new offerings on the altar, the first-fruits of the produce, to Yahuah (God), an heifer and a goat and a sheep on the altar as a burnt sacrifice to Yahuah (God); their fruit-offerings and their drink-offerings he offered upon the altar with frankincense.
And Yahuah (God) appeared to Abram, and said to him: “I am El Shaddai (God Almighty); approve yourself before Me and be you perfect.
And I will make My covenant between Me and you, and I will multiply you exceedingly.”

And Abram fell on his face, and Elohim (God) talked with him, and said: "Behold My ordinance is with you, And you will be the father of many nations. Neither will your name any more be called Abram, But your name from henceforth, even for ever, shall be Abraham. For the father of many nations have I made you. And I shall make you very great, And I shall make you into nations, And kings will come forth from you. And I shall establish My covenant between Me and you, and your seed after you, throughout their generations, for an eternal covenant, so that I may be a Elohim (God) to you, and to your seed after you.
(And I shall give to you and to your seed after you) the land where you have been a sojourner, the land of Canaan, that you may possess it for ever, and I shall be their Elohim (God)."

And Yahuah (God) said to Abraham: "And as for you, do you keep My Covenant, you and your seed after you, and circumcise you every male among you, and circumcise your foreskins, and it will be a token of an eternal covenant between Me and you.

And the child on the eighth day you will circumcise, every male throughout your generations, him that is born in the house, or whom you have bought with money from any stranger, whom you have acquired who is not of your seed.

He that is born in your house will surely be circumcised, and those whom you have bought with money will be circumcised, and My covenant will be in your flesh for an eternal ordinance. And the uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin on the eighth day, that soul will be cut off from his people, for he has broken My covenant."
And Elohim (God) said to Abraham: “As for Sarai your wife, her name will no more be called Sarai, but Sarah will be her name.
And I shall bless her, and give you a son by her, and I shall bless him, and he will become a nation, and kings of nations will proceed from him.”
And Abraham fell on his face, and rejoiced, and said in his heart: “Shall a son be born to him that is a hundred years old, and shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bring forth?”

And Abraham said to Elohim (God): “O that Ishmael might live before you!” And Elohim (God) said: “Yea, and Sarah also will bear you a son, and you will call his name Isaac, and I shall establish My covenant with him, an everlasting covenant, and for his seed after him.
And as for Ishmael also have I heard you, and behold I shall bless him, and make him great, and multiply him exceedingly, and he will beget twelve princes, and I shall make him a great nation.
But My covenant shall I establish with Isaac, whom Sarah will bear to you, in these days, in the next year.”
And He left off speaking with him, and Elohim (God) went up from Abraham.

And Abraham did according as Elohim (God) had said to him, and he took Ishmael his son, and all that were born in his house, and whom he had bought with his money, every male in his house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin. And on the selfsame day was Abraham circumcised, and all the men of his house, (and those born in the house), and all those, whom he had bought with money from the children of the stranger, were circumcised with him.

This law is for all the generations for ever, and there is no circumcision of the days, and no omission of one day out of the eight days; for it is an eternal ordinance, ordained and written on the heavenly tables.

And every one that is born, the flesh of whose foreskin is not circumcised on the eighth day, belongs not to the children of the covenant which Yahuah (God) made with Abraham, but to the children of destruction; nor is there, moreover, any sign on him that he is Yahuah (God)’s, but (he is destined) to be destroyed and slain from the earth, and to be rooted out of the earth, for he has broken the covenant of Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God).

For all the angels of the presence and all the angels of sanctification have been so created from the day of their creation, and before the angels of the presence and the angels of sanctification He has sanctified Yashar’el (Israel), that they should be with Him and with His holy angels.

And do you command the children of Yashar’el (Israel) and let them observe the sign of this covenant for their generations as an eternal ordinance, and they will not be rooted out of the land. For the command is ordained for a covenant, that they should observe it for ever among all the children of Yashar’el (Israel).

For Ishmael and his sons and his brothers and Esau, Yahuah (God) did not cause to approach Him, and he chose them not because they are the children of Abraham, because He knew them, but He chose Yashar’el (Israel) to be His people.

And He sanctified it, and gathered it from amongst all the children of men ; for there are many nations and many peoples, and all are His, and over all has He placed spirits in authority to lead them astray from Him.

But over Yashar’el (Israel) He did not appoint any angel or spirit, for He alone is their ruler, and He will preserve them and require them at the hand of His angels and His spirits, and at the hand of all His powers in order that He may preserve them and bless them, and that they may be His and He may be theirs from henceforth for ever.

And now I announce to you that the children of Yashar’el (Israel) will not keep true to this ordinance, and they will not circumcise their sons according to all this law; for in the flesh of their circumcision they will omit this circumcision of their sons, and all of them, sons of Beliar, will leave their sons uncircumcised as they were born. And there will be great wrath from Yahuah (God) against the children of Yashar’el (Israel), because they have forsaken His covenant and turned aside from His word, and provoked and blasphemed, inasmuch as they do not observe the ordinance of this law; for they have treated their members like the nations, so that they may be removed and rooted out of the land. And there will no more be pardon or forgiveness to them so that there should be forgiveness and pardon for all the sin of this eternal error.

chapters.commentary: The chapter opens with Abram celebrating the feast of the first-fruits of the grain harvest in the third month — Shavuot, the feast that chapter 6 said was kept in heaven from creation and on earth by Noah. Abram is keeping the feast, and the chapter notes it because in the middle of his keeping, Yahuah (God) appears: I am El Shaddai (God Almighty); approve yourself before Me and be you perfect. The covenant-name El Shaddai (God Almighty) enters the book here. Abram’s name becomes Abraham. Sarai’s name becomes Sarah. The promise of Isaac is given. And then the sign of the covenant is given in the flesh: every male circumcised on the eighth day, throughout the generations, as a token of an eternal covenant. The chapter is at pains to put circumcision in its right place. The promise was given in chapter 14. Faith was reckoned for righteousness in chapter 14. Then the sign was instituted in chapter 15. The order is the entire Pauline argument compressed into the source it is drawn from. Cometh this blessedness then upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? for we say that faith was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness. How was it then reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision. And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised (Romans 4:9–11). Paul did not invent this sequence. Paul read the text Jubilees preserves. The order is in the source. What Paul rebuts in Galatians is what the Judaizers did with this sequence — they inverted it. They said: circumcision first, as the mechanism of justification, and the believing scattered seed of Yashar’el (Israel) had to come into the covenant the same way the proselyte had always come in. The Judaizer error was not Torah- keeping. The Judaizer error was making the flesh-credential of circumcision the gate of justification, the very inversion Romans 4 and Galatians 3 dismantle. Paul, the Torah-observant Israelite of the tribe of Benjamin who circumcised Timothy and took Nazarite vows and went into the Temple in Acts 21, was not against the sign. He was against the inversion. Jubilees 15 is the chapter that holds the sequence right. Read it carefully and the Pauline argument is no longer a paradox. It is a defense of what Jubilees already taught. Verse 30 is the chapter’s hard word, and it is the verse that forces the reader to keep the three categories straight. For Ishmael and his sons and his brothers and Esau, Yahuah (God) did not cause to approach Him, and he chose them not because they are the children of Abraham, because He knew them, but He chose Yashar’el (Israel) to be His people. Two things to register. First, the elect line is not all the descendants of Abraham; the elect line narrows further still, to Isaac and not Ishmael, to Jacob and not Esau, and only inside that narrowed line is Yashar’el (Israel) chosen. The bloodline matters and the bloodline narrows. Second, the choice of Yashar’el (Israel) is not a denial of the Father’s care for the nations. Verse 31: for there are many nations and many peoples, and all are His, and over all has He placed spirits in authority to lead them astray from Him. The nations are His — they belong to him — but they are placed under intermediary authorities, and the special distinction of Yashar’el (Israel) is that over Yashar’el (Israel) He did not appoint any angel or spirit, for He alone is their ruler. This is the verse the inclusion gospels in every house need to soften and the verse the foundational lie of every house needs to deny. Christianity says: the church replaced this distinction. Hebrew roots says: anyone who keeps Torah inherits this distinction. Judaism says: this distinction is Yahudah’s (Judah’s) alone. Islam says: this distinction transferred to Ishmael. All four denials. All four installations of something else in Yashar’el’s (Israel’s) place. Jubilees 15:30–31 is the verse that makes all four denials demonstrably wrong. The covenant people are who Yahuah (God) said they were: the seed of Jacob, the twelve tribes, the firstborn son of Yahuah (God), under his direct rule and not under intermediaries. The scattering of the ten tribes through exile did not dissolve them. The dispersion of Yahudim (Jews) through diaspora did not dissolve them. The covenant body is being gathered, and the gathering is what Jubilees 1 promised at the beginning of the book. Verse 33 closes the chapter with the prophecy that Yashar’el (Israel) itself will not keep the sign — they will leave their sons uncircumcised as they were born, all of them, sons of Beliar. The sign of the covenant will be abandoned by the covenant body before the prophets ever speak. The forgetting that runs through every chapter so far runs through this one too. The recovery the Father is working in his scattered seed today includes the recovery of the sign. The Christian who has been told that the sign was abolished and that circumcision of the heart abolished circumcision of the flesh is reading the chapter exactly upside down. Both are commanded. Both are kept. The heart’s circumcision is what makes the flesh’s circumcision honest. Neither stands alone. Jubilees keeps them together; Christianity has been pulling them apart for seventeen centuries.

chapters.title: Sodom and the Birth of Isaac

verses.text: And on the new moon of the fourth month we appeared to Abraham, at the oak of Mamre, and we talked with him, and we announced to him that a son would be given to him by Sarah his wife.
And Sarah laughed, for she heard that we had spoken these words with Abraham, and we admonished her, and she became afraid, and denied that she had laughed on account of the words.
And we told her the name of her son, as his name is ordained and written in the heavenly tables (i.e.) Isaac.
And (that) when we returned to her at a set time, she would have conceived a son.

And in this month Yahuah (God) executed his judgments on Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Zeboim, and all the region of the Jordan, and He burned them with fire and brimstone, and destroyed them until this day, even as lo I have declared to you all their works, that they are wicked and sinners exceedingly, and that they defile themselves and commit fornication in their flesh, and work uncleanness on the earth.

And, in like manner, Elohim (God) will execute judgment on the places where they have done according to the uncleanness of the Sodomites, like to the judgment of Sodom. But Lot we saved; for Elohim (God) remembered Abraham, and sent him out from the midst of the overthrow.
