The Egyptian regime sees the orientation and decides to break it by labor. The reader is being shown an early version of a pattern the prophets will name later. A regime detects that the covenant body’s heart is elsewhere; the regime cannot tolerate this; the regime imposes labor to break the heart’s orientation. The same pattern operates in any age. The institutional system that detects the awakening remnant’s heart turning toward the Sabbath, the festivals, the sacred names, the prophetic gathering, the Father’s actual ordering of the calendar — that system, of any of the four houses, will move from welcome to suspicion to pressure. The pressure is not the failure of the awakening remnant. The pressure is the regime’s acknowledgment that the heart has, in fact, turned. The chapter is preparing the reader for that pressure by showing the original of it. The Egyptian regime did not break the body. The body multiplied under the affliction. And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied. Verse 15. The chapter’s last word on the oppression is that it failed. The body grew under the iron furnace.

chapters.title: The Childhood of Moses

verses.text: And in the seventh week, in the seventh year, in the forty-seventh jubilee, your father went forth from the land of Canaan, and you were born in the fourth week, in the sixth year thereof, in the forty-eighth jubilee; this was the time of tribulation on the children of Yashar’el (Israel).
And Pharaoh, king of Egypt, issued a command regarding them that they should cast all their male children which were born into the river.
And they cast them in for seven months until the day that you were born. And your mother hid you for three months, and they told regarding her.

And she made an ark for you, and covered it with pitch and asphalt, and placed it in the flags on the bank of the river, and she placed you in it seven days, and your mother came by night and suckled you, and by day Miriam, your sister, guarded you from the birds.
And in those days Tharmuth, the daughter of Pharaoh, came to bathe in the river, and she heard your voice crying, and she told her maidens to bring you forth, and they brought you to her.

And she took you out of the ark, and she had compassion on you. And your sister said to her: “Shall I go and call to you one of the Hebrew women to nurse and suckle this babe for you?” And she said (to her): “Go.”
And she went and called your mother Jochebed, and she gave her wages, and she nursed you.

And afterwards, when you were grown up, they brought you to the daughter of Pharaoh, and you did become her son, and Amram your father taught you writing, and after you had completed three weeks they brought you into the royal court.

And you were three weeks of years at court until the time when you did go forth from the royal court and did see an Egyptian smiting your friend who was of the children of Yashar’el (Israel), and you did slay him and hide him in the sand.

And on the second day you did find two of the children of Yashar’el (Israel) striving together, and you did say to him who was doing the wrong: "Why do you smite your brother? And he was angry and indignant, and said “Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Thinkest you to kill me as you killedst the Egyptian yesterday?” And you did fear and flee on account of these words.

chapters.commentary: The chapter switches voice. The angel of the presence, who has been narrating to Moses since chapter 1, addresses Moses directly and recounts Moses’ own birth. Your father went forth from the land of Canaan, and you were born in the fourth week, in the sixth year thereof, in the forty-eighth jubilee; this was the time of tribulation on the children of Yashar’el (Israel). Verse 1. The deliverer is born in the time of tribulation. The chapter does not separate the two facts; it joins them. The pattern of the deliverer arriving inside the suffering, not after it, is what Jubilees is naming. The covenant body does not wait for the suffering to end before the deliverer comes; the deliverer comes in the suffering, hidden in the household, in the pitch-and-asphalt ark in the river of death. The reader who has been told that the gathering of the scattered seed will only come after the awakening remnant has secured its footing is being shown that the deliverer’s pattern is the opposite. He arrives in the storm. He is hidden during it. He grows up inside the apparatus of the oppressor — they brought you to her… and you became her son, and Amram your father taught you writing — and he is positioned exactly where he can act when the moment is given. The deliverer is hidden three months in his mother’s house, then seven days in the ark on the bank of the river. Your mother came by night and suckled you, and by day Miriam, your sister, guarded you from the birds. Verse 4. The covenant body’s deliverer is preserved by the courage of the women — the mother who hides him, the sister who guards him, the daughter of Pharaoh who pulls him out. Three women. Three layers of protection. The chapter is repeating the pattern of Tamar in chapter 41 and Sarah and Rebecca in earlier chapters: when the men’s arrangements have been broken by oppression, the women step in and the deliverer comes through their hands. Moses is brought back to Jochebed his mother for nursing — she gave her wages, and she nursed you — and the deliverer drinks the milk of his covenant mother under contract from the daughter of the oppressor. The household that Pharaoh thought it was extending — the privilege of nursing the prince at imperial expense — was actually the covenant body raising its deliverer at the oppressor’s expense. The chapter is not subtle about whose plan was operating. And Amram your father taught you writing, and after you had completed three weeks they brought you into the royal court. Verse 9. Three weeks is twenty-one years. Moses is taught writing by his Levite father — Hebrew writing, the writing of the patriarchal library — for the first twenty-one years of his life. Then he is brought to the royal court for the next twenty-one years. The deliverer’s education is half-and-half: half covenant scribal, half imperial administrative. The pattern matters. The reader who has been told that the awakening believer must abandon every part of the system they came out of is being shown a different pattern. Moses kept his Hebrew writing across his Egyptian education. He did not lose his patriarchal library when he went into the court. The chapter is implying that the deliverer is the one who can speak the language of both, and that the covenant body’s children, in any age, are not required to dispose of every imperial competence they acquired during the time of oppression. Moses will write the Torah. The writing he writes it in is the writing his father taught him in the household before the court ever saw him. The covenant body is literate in its own scripture before it is literate in the empire’s administrative system, and the order is the chapter’s quiet load. Verses 10–12 narrate the slaying of the Egyptian and the flight to Midian. You did slay him and hide him in the sand. And on the second day you did find two of the children of Yashar’el (Israel) striving together, and you did say to him who was doing the wrong: “Why do you smite your brother?” The chapter does not soften the killing. Moses struck and slew. The chapter also does not soften Moses’ interjection on the second day: why do you smite your brother? The deliverer’s first instinct, before the calling has been fully given, is to correct violence inside the covenant body and to act against violence from outside the body. Both instincts are right. Both instincts will be matured at the burning bush. The chapter ends with Moses fleeing Egypt because his slaying of the Egyptian has become known. The deliverer goes into the desert. The chapter closes on the flight. The next chapter will pick up at the burning bush and the return.

chapters.title: From Midian to the Exodus

verses.text: And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.
And you yourself know what He spake to you on Mount Sinai, and what prince Mastêmâ desired to do with you when you were returning into Egypt on the way when you did meet him at the lodging-place.
Did he not with all his power seek to slay you and deliver the Egyptians out of your hand when he saw that you were sent to execute judgment and vengeance on the Egyptians?

And I delivered you out of his hand, and you did perform the signs and wonders which you were sent to perform in Egypt against Pharaoh, and against all his house, and against his servants and his people.

And Yahuah (God) executed a great vengeance on them for Yashar’el’s (Israel’s) sake, and smote them through (the plagues of) blood and frogs, lice and dog-flies, and malignant boils breaking forth in blains; and their cattle by death; and by hail-stones, thereby He destroyed everything that grew for them; and by locusts which devoured the residue which had been left by the hail, and by darkness; and (by the death) of the first-born of men and animals, and on all their idols Yahuah (God) took vengeance and burned them with fire.
And everything was sent through your hand, that you should declare (these things) before they were done, and you did speak with the king of Egypt before all his servants and before his people.

And everything took place according to your words; ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt that you might execute vengeance on it for Yashar’el (Israel). And Yahuah (God) did everything for Yashar’el’s (Israel’s) sake, and according to His covenant, which He had ordained with Abraham that He would take vengeance on them as they had brought them by force into bondage.
And the prince of the Mastêmâ stood up against you, and sought to cast you into the hands of Pharaoh, and he helped the Egyptian sorcerers, and they stood up and wrought before you.
The evils indeed we permitted them to work, but the remedies we did not allow to be wrought by their hands.
And Yahuah (God) smote them with malignant ulcers, and they were not able to stand for we destroyed them so that they could not perform a single sign.

And notwithstanding all (these) signs and wonders the prince of the Mastêmâ was not put to shame because he took courage and cried to the Egyptians to pursue after you with all the powers of the Egyptians, with their chariots, and with their horses, and with all the hosts of the peoples of Egypt. And I stood between the Egyptians and Yashar’el (Israel), and we delivered Yashar’el (Israel) out of his hand, and out of the hand of his people, and Yahuah (God) brought them through the midst of the sea as if it were dry land.

And all the peoples whom he brought to pursue after Yashar’el (Israel), Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) cast them into the midst of the sea, into the depths of the abyss beneath the children of Yashar’el (Israel), even as the people of Egypt had cast their children into the river. He took vengeance on 1,000,000 of them, and one thousand strong and energetic men were destroyed on account of one suckling of the children of your people which they had thrown into the river.

And on the fourteenth day and on the fifteenth and on the sixteenth and on the seventeenth and on the eighteenth the prince of the Mastêmâ was bound and imprisoned behind the children of Yashar’el (Israel) that he might not accuse them.
And on the nineteenth we let them loose that they might help the Egyptians and pursue the children of Yashar’el (Israel).

And he hardened their hearts and made them stubborn, and the device was devised by Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) that He might smite the Egyptians and cast them into the sea. And on the fourteenth we bound him that he might not accuse the children of Yashar’el (Israel) on the day when they asked the Egyptians for vessels and garments, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of bronze, in order to despoil the Egyptians in return for the bondage in which they had forced them to serve.
And we did not lead forth the children of Yashar’el (Israel) from Egypt empty handed.

chapters.commentary: In the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee. Verse 1. The chapter compresses Exodus 2–14 into nineteen verses. Jubilees does not narrate the burning bush encounter; it assumes the reader knows it. What Jubilees adds is the Mastema architecture, the binding-and-loosing of the prince of Mastema during the plagues, and the count of the pursuit at the sea. Verse 2 is the pivotal addition Jubilees inserts that Exodus does not. Prince Mastêmâ desired to do with you when you were returning into Egypt on the way when you did meet him at the lodging-place. Did he not with all his power seek to slay you and deliver the Egyptians out of your hand when he saw that you were sent to execute judgment and vengeance on the Egyptians? The mysterious passage of Exodus 4:24 — And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that Yahuah (God) met him, and sought to kill him — is the same encounter Jubilees is recounting, but the assailant is named. Prince Mastêmâ. Not Yahuah (God). The Christian reading that has had to make sense of Exodus 4:24 by deciding that Yahuah (God) was angry with Moses for failing to circumcise his son is dismantled here. The angry party was the prince of Mastema, the spirit-accuser of the covenant body, who detected that Moses was being sent to break Egypt and tried to kill him before he could begin. Zipporah’s circumcision of the son appeases the demand of the moment by satisfying the covenant requirement that Mastema was using as his ground for the attack. The chapter is helping the reader read Exodus 4 with the right party named. Yahuah (God) is the deliverer; Mastema is the accuser. The distinction has been the book’s spine since chapter 10. Verses 5–8 list the plagues. Blood and frogs, lice and dog-flies, and malignant boils breaking forth in blains; and their cattle by death; and by hail-stones… and by locusts… and by darkness; and (by the death) of the first-born of men and animals. Verse 7: ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt that you might execute vengeance on it for Yashar’el (Israel). The chapter names the count — ten — and the cause — vengeance for Yashar’el (Israel). Pause on the cause. The plagues were not educational demonstrations. They were judicial. Egypt had cast Yashar’el’s (Israel’s) children into the river; the plagues returned, in tenfold form, what Egypt had done. And on all their idols Yahuah (God) took vengeance and burned them with fire. Verse 5. The plagues were also a polemic against the Egyptian pantheon. Each plague struck at one of the cult-figures Egypt had exalted: the Nile (Hapi), the frogs (Heqet), the cattle (Apis), the sun (Ra), and so on. The covenant body was being shown, through the plagues, that the formed Word who had brought them out had authority over every named power of the imperial cult. Jubilees does not catalogue the polemic verse by verse, but the framing — on all their idols Yahuah (God) took vengeance — gives the reader the grid. Verses 9–14 narrate the Mastema architecture during the exodus itself. The prince of the Mastêmâ stood up against you, and sought to cast you into the hands of Pharaoh, and he helped the Egyptian sorcerers, and they stood up and wrought before you. The evils indeed we permitted them to work, but the remedies we did not allow to be wrought by their hands. The pattern Jubilees has been building is now sharpened. The accuser cannot operate without permission. The remedies are reserved for Yahuah’s (God’s) hand. Verse 11: Yahuah (God) smote them with malignant ulcers, and they were not able to stand for we destroyed them so that they could not perform a single sign. The Egyptian sorcerers are taken out by the sixth plague. The accuser’s tools fail. The covenant body’s deliverer operates uncontested. Verses 15–18 give the choreography of the binding. On the fourteenth day and on the fifteenth and on the sixteenth and on the seventeenth and on the eighteenth the prince of the Mastêmâ was bound and imprisoned behind the children of Yashar’el (Israel) that he might not accuse them. And on the nineteenth we let them loose that they might help the Egyptians and pursue the children of Yashar’el (Israel). And he hardened their hearts and made them stubborn, and the device was devised by Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) that He might smite the Egyptians and cast them into the sea. And on the fourteenth we bound him that he might not accuse the children of Yashar’el (Israel) on the day when they asked the Egyptians for vessels and garments, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of bronze, in order to despoil the Egyptians in return for the bondage in which they had forced them to serve. And we did not lead forth the children of Yashar’el (Israel) from Egypt empty handed. Five days the prince of Mastema is bound — the fourteenth (the day of the Passover) through the eighteenth — so that the despoiling of Egypt and the passage of the sea may be accomplished without accusation. The accuser is bound, not erased. On the nineteenth he is released so that the device of Pharaoh’s pursuit can be drawn through to the sea. The chapter is showing the reader that even the hardening of Pharaoh’s heart is held inside this architecture: the accuser is permitted to work where Yahuah (God) is using the work to draw the judgment to the right geography. The covenant body did not despoil Egypt in defiance of a free-actor accuser; the covenant body despoiled Egypt during the window in which the accuser was bound. The reader who has been told that the despoiling was a moral problem — that Yashar’el (Israel) “stole” from the Egyptians — is being shown the chapter’s correction. We did not lead forth the children of Yashar’el (Israel) from Egypt empty handed. The vessels were not stolen; they were back-payment for four hundred and thirty years of unpaid labor. The covenant body left with the wages it had earned. The architecture of the despoiling is therefore covenantal, not predatory. Yahuah (God) had told Abraham in chapter 14 that his seed would come out with great possessions. The chapter records the keeping of the promise. The crossing of the sea is two verses. I stood between the Egyptians and Yashar’el (Israel), and we delivered Yashar’el (Israel) out of his hand, and out of the hand of his people, and Yahuah (God) brought them through the midst of the sea as if it were dry land. And all the peoples whom he brought to pursue after Yashar’el (Israel), Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) cast them into the midst of the sea, into the depths of the abyss beneath the children of Yashar’el (Israel), even as the people of Egypt had cast their children into the river. He took vengeance on 1,000,000 of them, and one thousand strong and energetic men were destroyed on account of one suckling of the children of your people which they had thrown into the river. Verses 13–14. The math Jubilees gives is precise and brutal: a thousand Egyptian fighters for one Hebrew infant cast in the Nile. The pattern of judicial return is held all the way through. The Father exacts what he exacts. The Egyptian lives lost are not a tragic incident in a liberation narrative; they are the just payment of a debt the Egyptian cult had been incurring for centuries. The chapter is clear-eyed.

chapters.title: The Passover

verses.text: Remember the commandment which Yahuah (God) commanded you concerning the passover, that you should celebrate it in its season on the fourteenth of the first month, that you should kill it before it is evening, and that they should eat it by night on the evening of the fifteenth from the time of the setting of the sun.

For on this night–the beginning of the festival and the beginning of the joy–you were eating the passover in Egypt, when all the powers of Mastêmâ had been let loose to slay all the first-born in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh to the first-born of the captive maidservant in the mill, and to the cattle.

And this is the sign which Yahuah (God) gave them: Into every house on the lintels of which they saw the blood of a lamb of the first year, into (that) house they should not enter to slay, but should pass by (it), that all those should be saved that were in the house because the sign of the blood was on its lintels.

And the powers of Yahuah (God) did everything according as Yahuah (God) commanded them, and they passed by all the children of Yashar’el (Israel), and the plague came not upon them to destroy from amongst them any soul either of cattle, or man, or dog.
And the plague was very grievous in Egypt, and there was no house in Egypt where there was not one dead, and weeping and lamentation.

And all Yashar’el (Israel) was eating the flesh of the paschal lamb, and drinking the wine, and was lauding and blessing, and giving thanks to Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers, and was ready to go forth from under the yoke of Egypt; and from the evil bondage. And remember you this day all the days of your life, and observe it from year to year all the days of your life, once a year, on its day, according to all the law thereof, and do not adjourn (it) from day to day, or from month to month.

For it is an eternal ordinance, and engraven on the heavenly tables regarding all the children of Yashar’el (Israel) that they should observe it every year on its day once a year, throughout all their generations; and there is no limit of days, for this is ordained for ever.

And the man who is free from uncleanness, and does not come to observe it on occasion of its day, so as to bring an acceptable offering before Yahuah (God), and to eat and to drink before Yahuah (God) on the day of its festival, that man who is clean and close at hand will be cut off; because he offered not the oblation of Yahuah (God) in its appointed season, he will take the guilt upon himself.

Let the children of Yashar’el (Israel) come and observe the passover on the day of its fixed time, on the fourteenth day of the first month, between the evenings, from the third part of the day to the third part of the night, for two portions of the day are given to the light, and a third part to the evening.

That is that which Yahuah (God) commanded you that you should observe it between the evenings. And it is not permissible to slay it during any period of the light, but during the period bordering on the evening, and let them eat it at the time of the evening until the third part of the night, and whatever is leftover of all its flesh from the third part of the night and onwards, let them burn it with fire.

And they shall not cook it with water, nor shall they eat it raw, but roast on the fire: they shall eat it with diligence, its head with the inwards thereof and its feet they shall roast with fire, and not break any bone thereof; for of the children of Yashar’el (Israel) no bone shall be crushed.

For this reason Yahuah (God) commanded the children of Yashar’el (Israel) to observe the passover on the day of its fixed time, and they shall not break a bone thereof; for it is a festival day, and a day commanded, and there may be no passing over from day to day, and month to month, but on the day of its festival let it be observed.

And do you command the children of Yashar’el (Israel) to observe the passover throughout their days, every year, once a year on the day of its fixed time, and it will come for a memorial well pleasing before Yahuah (God), and no plague will come upon them to slay or to smite in that year in which they celebrate the passover in its season in every respect according to His command.

And they shall not eat it outside the sanctuary of Yahuah (God), but before the sanctuary of Yahuah (God), and all the people of the congregation of Yashar’el (Israel) shall celebrate it in its appointed season. And every man who has come upon its day shall eat it in the sanctuary of your Elohim (God) before Yahuah (God) from twenty years old and upward; for thus is it written and ordained that they should eat it in the sanctuary of Yahuah (God).

And when the children of Yashar’el (Israel) come into the land which they are to possess, into the land of Canaan, and set up the tabernacle of Yahuah (God) in the midst of the land in one of their tribes until the sanctuary of Yahuah (God) has been built in the land, let them come and celebrate the passover in the midst of the tabernacle of Yahuah (God), and let them slay it before Yahuah (God) from year to year.

And in the days when the house has been built in the name of Yahuah (God) in the land of their inheritance, they shall go there and slay the passover in the evening, at sunset, at the third part of the day.

And they will offer its blood on the threshold of the altar, and shall place its fat on the fire which is upon the altar, and they shall eat its flesh roasted with fire in the court of the house which has been sanctified in the name of Yahuah (God).

And they may not celebrate the passover in their cities, 1 nor in any place save before the tabernacle of Yahuah (God), or before His house where His name has dwelt; and they will not go astray from Yahuah (God). And do you, Moses, command the children of Yashar’el (Israel) to observe the ordinances of the passover, as it was commanded to you; declare you to them every year and the day of its days, and 2 the festival of unleavened bread, that they should eat unleavened bread seven days, (and) that they should observe its festival, and that they bring an oblation every day during those seven days of joy before Yahuah (God) on the altar of your Elohim (God).
For you celebrated this festival with haste 3 when you went forth from Egypt till you entered into the wilderness of Shur; 4 for on the shore of the sea you completed it.

chapters.commentary: Remember the commandment which Yahuah (God) commanded you concerning the passover, that you should celebrate it in its season on the fourteenth of the first month, that you should kill it before it is evening, and that they should eat it by night on the evening of the fifteenth from the time of the setting of the sun. Verse 1. The chapter is the most concentrated halakhic block in the entire book. Jubilees is not narrating the Passover in chapter 49; it is prescribing it, in detail, to be kept by Yashar’el (Israel) throughout the generations. Verses 1–6 set the original Passover scene. The blood on the lintels. The plague that strikes every Egyptian house. The children of Yashar’el (Israel) was eating the flesh of the paschal lamb, and drinking the wine, and was lauding and blessing, and giving thanks to Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers, and was ready to go forth from under the yoke of Egypt; and from the evil bondage. The covenant body in Egypt at the Passover is depicted eating, drinking, blessing, and ready. The chapter is showing what the practice of the festival is: not solemn lament but prepared rejoicing. The covenant body, on the night of judgment, eats and drinks and blesses Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) and is ready. The pattern is the festival’s template across the centuries. Verses 7–9 give the standing ordinance. Remember you this day all the days of your life, and observe it from year to year all the days of your life, once a year, on its day, according to all the law thereof, and do not adjourn (it) from day to day, or from month to month. For it is an eternal ordinance, and engraven on the heavenly tables regarding all the children of Yashar’el (Israel) that they should observe it every year on its day once a year, throughout all their generations; and there is no limit of days, for this is ordained for ever. Pause on what Jubilees claims for the Passover. Eternal ordinance. Engraven on the heavenly tables. No limit of days. Ordained for ever. The Passover is not a Mosaic addition that the cross has retired. The Passover, in Jubilees’ framing, is on the heavenly tables before Sinai, given to Yashar’el (Israel) at Sinai, and held without any expiration clause across the generations. The Christian habit of teaching that the Passover was fulfilled in the bread-and-wine memorial — what later Christianity called the Lord’s Supper — and is therefore no longer for the body to keep, is the reading the chapter is dismantling four jubilees before that later memorial even exists. The Passover is not retired. The Passover is what the body does once a year forever. The 1234 of Truth applies. He that says I know him and keeps not his commandments is a liar. The Passover is one of the commandments. A teaching that says the body of the Messiah (Christ) does not keep the Passover, while claiming to know the Messiah (Christ), is the line the 1234 of Truth filter rejects. The chapter does not argue this; it states the architecture and lets the architecture speak. Verses 10–14 detail the timing and the prohibitions. Between the evenings, from the third part of the day to the third part of the night, for two portions of the day are given to the light, and a third part to the evening. Specific. Slay it during the period bordering on the evening, and let them eat it at the time of the evening until the third part of the night, and whatever is leftover of all its flesh from the third part of the night and onwards, let them burn it with fire. Specific. They shall not cook it with water, nor shall they eat it raw, but roast on the fire: they shall eat it with diligence, its head with the inwards thereof and its feet they shall roast with fire, and not break any bone thereof; for of the children of Yashar’el (Israel) no bone shall be crushed. Verse 13. The phrase Jubilees uses — no bone shall be crushed — is the same phrase John 19:36 will quote at the cross. For these things were done, that the scripture should be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken. The line is older than Sinai; it is engraven on the heavenly tables; it is fulfilled in Yahusha (Jesus) at the cross because the cross is the antitype of what Jubilees calls the eternal ordinance. The Passover lamb is the type. Yahusha (Jesus) is the antitype. The type does not retire when the antitype arrives. Yahusha (Jesus) himself kept the Passover the night before he died, instituted the bread-and-cup as the Passover-meal he was that very night fulfilling, and his body answered to the bone-not-broken clause of Jubilees 49. The continuity is total. The covenant body is to keep the Passover. Verses 15–17 add the once-a-year and the location. Every man who has come upon its day shall eat it in the sanctuary of your Elohim (God) before Yahuah (God) from twenty years old and upward; for thus is it written and ordained that they should eat it in the sanctuary of Yahuah (God). The Passover, in Jubilees’ framing, must be kept at the sanctuary. After the destruction of the second temple, this part of the prescription has not been keepable in its fullness. The book is honest about the architecture: where the sanctuary is, the Passover is kept there; until the sanctuary is, the body keeps what it can keep of the Passover where it is. This is not a license to abolish the festival; it is a recognition that the body has been in a long exile in which the full keeping is unavailable. The body keeps what is keepable, marks the date, eats the lamb (or the substitute the rabbinic tradition has held), and remembers. The gathering at the end of the age — the gathering the prophets named — is the time when the Passover will again be kept in its full geography, in the sanctuary of Yahuah (God) in the land. Until then, the body does what it can, on the day, every year, with old grain when the new is not there. A further note. The Passover the covenant body kept on the night of the exodus was not just a meal. It was the occasion of the binding of the prince of Mastema (chapter 48 already named the binding window — the fourteenth through the eighteenth). The Passover is therefore tied to the architecture of the accuser being bound. When the body keeps the Passover in its season, in the sanctuary or as near to the sanctuary as it can, the architecture the Father set in place at the original Passover is re-engaged. The body’s keeping of the festival is not symbolic remembrance; it is participation in an architecture that is still running. The reader is not being told to do anything other than hear what the chapter is saying about its own keeping. The chapter is not a how-to. The chapter is showing the reader why the festival was given the way it was given. What the reader does with that knowledge, between the reader and the Father, is between the reader and the Father. The chapter closes with the seven-day festival of unleavened bread that follows the Passover (verse 22) and the haste of the original exodus (verse 23). You celebrated this festival with haste when you went forth from Egypt till you entered into the wilderness of Shur; for on the shore of the sea you completed it. The original keeping ran from the lamb on the fourteenth through the seven days of unleavened bread, ending at the shore of the sea after the crossing. The festival is structurally tied to the deliverance and the covenant body’s first vindicated standing on the far side of the sea. The covenant body’s annual return to this festival is its annual reorientation to the architecture of deliverance — a deliverance that is not yet complete because the full gathering has not yet happened. The festival is the body’s annual statement that the Father did this once, and the Father will do it again, and the body is keeping the count.

chapters.title: The Sabbaths and the Jubilees

verses.text: And after this law I made known to you the days of the Sabbaths in the desert of Sinai, which is between Elim and Sinai.

And I told you of the Sabbaths of the land on Mount Sinai, and I told you of the jubilee years in the sabbaths of years: but the year thereof have I not told you till you enter the land which you are to possess.
And the land also will keep its sabbaths while they dwell upon it, and they will know the jubilee year.

Wherefore I have ordained for you the year-weeks and the years and the jubilees: there are forty-nine jubilees from the days of Adam until this day, and one week and two years and there are yet forty years to come (lit. "distant for learning the commandments of Yahuah (God), until they pass over into the land of Canaan, crossing the Jordan to the west.

And the jubilees will pass by, until Yashar’el (Israel) is cleansed from all guilt of fornication, and uncleanness, and pollution, and sin, and error, and dwells with confidence in all the land, and there will be no more a Satan or any evil one, and the land will be clean from that time for evermore. And behold the commandment regarding the Sabbaths–I have written (them) down for you and all the judgments of its laws.

Six days will you labour, but on the seventh day is the Sabbath of Yahuah your Elohim (the LORD your God). In it you shall do no manner of work, you and your sons, and your men-servants and your maid-servants, and all your cattle and the sojourner also who is with you.

And the man that does any work on it shall die: whoever desecrates that day, whoever lies with (his) wife or whoever says he will do something on it, that he will set out on a journey thereon in regard to any buying or selling: and whoever draws water thereon which he had not prepared for himself on the sixth day, and whoever takes up any burden to carry it out of his tent or out of his house shall die.

You shall do no work whatever on the Sabbath day save that you have prepared for yourselves on the sixth day, so as to eat, and drink, and rest, and keep Sabbath from all work on that day, and to bless Yahuah your Elohim (the LORD your God), who has given you a day of festival, and a holy day: and a day of the holy kingdom for all Yashar’el (Israel) is this day among their days for ever.

For great is the honour which Yahuah (God) has given to Yashar’el (Israel) that they should eat and drink and be satisfied on this festival day, and rest thereon from all labour which belongs to the labour of the children of men, save burning frankincense and bringing oblations and sacrifices before Yahuah (God) for days and for Sabbaths. This work alone shall be done on the Sabbath-days in the sanctuary of Yahuah your Elohim (the LORD your God); that they may atone for Yashar’el (Israel) with sacrifice continually from day to day for a memorial well-pleasing before Yahuah (God), and that He may receive them always from day to day according as you have been commanded.

And every man who does any work thereon, or goes a journey, or tills (his) farm, whether in his house or any other place, and whoever lights a fire, or rides on any beast, or travels by ship on the sea, and whoever strikes or kills anything, or slaughters a beast or a bird, or whoever catches an animal or a bird or a fish, or whoever fasts or makes war on the Sabbaths:

The man who does any of these things on the Sabbath shall die, so that the children of Yashar’el (Israel) shall observe the Sabbaths according to the commandments regarding the Sabbaths of the land, as it is written in the tables, which He gave into my hands that I should write out for you the laws of the seasons, and the seasons according to the division of their days. Herewith is completed the account of the division of the days.

chapters.commentary: The book closes on the Sabbath. And after this law I made known to you the days of the Sabbaths in the desert of Sinai, which is between Elim and Sinai. And I told you of the Sabbaths of the land on Mount Sinai, and I told you of the jubilee years in the sabbaths of years. Verses 1–2. The closing chapter braids the three Sabbath rhythms the book has been teaching from chapter 2: the weekly Sabbath, the sabbatical year (Sabbath of the land), and the Jubilee year (Sabbath of sabbaths). The architecture is tri-partite. Each level is real. Each level is engraved on the heavenly tables. Each level is given to Yashar’el (Israel) to keep across the generations. Verse 4 is the chapter’s chronological seal. Wherefore I have ordained for you the year-weeks and the years and the jubilees: there are forty-nine jubilees from the days of Adam until this day, and one week and two years and there are yet forty years to come (lit. "distant for learning the commandments of Yahuah (God), until they pass over into the land of Canaan, crossing the Jordan to the west. Forty-nine jubilees from Adam to Sinai. The book’s whole structure has been counting toward this verse. The reader who has been told that the patriarchal chronology is decorative is being shown that the chronology is the book’s architecture. The forty-nine-jubilee count is not random. Forty-nine years is one Jubilee. Forty-nine Jubilees is the Jubilee of Jubilees. The covenant body at Sinai is, in Jubilees’ frame, standing at the Jubilee of Jubilees from Adam — the moment of the maximum reset, the moment when the heavenly architecture of liberation lands at full weight. The giving of the Torah at Sinai is, structurally, the largest Jubilee event the world has yet seen. The covenant body’s freedom from Egypt is paid out at the center of a fiftieth-Jubilee structure that has been counting since Adam. Verse 5 is the chapter’s prophetic frame. And the jubilees will pass by, until Yashar’el (Israel) is cleansed from all guilt of fornication, and uncleanness, and pollution, and sin, and error, and dwells with confidence in all the land, and there will be no more a Satan or any evil one, and the land will be clean from that time for evermore. The eschatological seal. The Jubilees keep counting. Yashar’el (Israel) is cleansed. The covenant body dwells with confidence in the whole land. The accuser is gone. The land is clean. For evermore. The book that opened with Yahuah (God) saying he would gather and circumcise the heart and plant the body as the plant of uprightness now closes with the same vision under its calendar. The architecture of chapter 1 is the architecture of chapter 50. The book is internally seamless. Verses 6–9 deliver the weekly-Sabbath halakha. Six days will you labour, but on the seventh day is the Sabbath of Yahuah your Elohim (the LORD your God). In it you shall do no manner of work, you and your sons, and your men-servants and your maid-servants, and all your cattle and the sojourner also who is with you. Verse 7. The sojourner is named. The Torah-stranger of chapter 30’s intermarriage block has the same Sabbath rest the covenant body has. The covenant household keeps the Sabbath together — sons, servants, cattle, sojourner. The pattern is the rest pattern of the universal seventh-day witness Isaiah 56 will later expand. And the man that does any work on it shall die. Verse 8. The chapter is severe. Jubilees does not soften the Sabbath ordinance. The death penalty for Sabbath violation is named twice (verses 8 and 13). The reader who has been told that Jubilees’ severity here is embarrassing — that no contemporary covenant body would actually apply a death penalty for picking up sticks on the Sabbath — needs to hear what the chapter is saying. The death penalty is a theological marker before it is a judicial procedure. The chapter is saying that Sabbath-breaking is, in the covenant body’s architecture, on the same level of severity as the things the death penalty was reserved for: idolatry, murder, false prophecy, treason. The Sabbath is that load-bearing. Christianity’s seventeen-century habit of treating the Sabbath as discretionary, moveable to the first day, replaceable with an hour of service — that habit, against the chapter’s explicit framing, can be read only one way. The Sabbath was not what was retired. The day-keeping was not what was abolished. The horn moved the day, and the horn’s move is what the chapter — and Daniel 7:25, and Mark 7:13, and Revelation 11:18 — names as the ground for the verdict. The list of forbidden Sabbath activities (verses 8–13) is exhaustive. Whoever lies with (his) wife or whoever says he will do something on it, that he will set out on a journey thereon in regard to any buying or selling: and whoever draws water thereon which he had not prepared for himself on the sixth day, and whoever takes up any burden to carry it out of his tent or out of his house… goes a journey, or tills (his) farm, whether in his house or any other place, and whoever lights a fire, or rides on any beast, or travels by ship on the sea, and whoever strikes or kills anything, or slaughters a beast or a bird, or whoever catches an animal or a bird or a fish, or whoever fasts or makes war on the Sabbaths. The list is the chapter’s most demanding paragraph. It is not for the reader to use as a checklist; it is for the reader to recognize. Jubilees is making the case that the Sabbath in the covenant body is total — household, animal, kindling, transport, commerce, hunting, fasting, war — and that the body’s keeping of the day is the body’s most public testimony that it knows whose day it is. The body that keeps a thinned-out Sabbath is admitting the day is not actually about anything in particular. The body that keeps it the way Jubilees describes is admitting that the day is the rest of Yahuah (God) and the body is the body that rests with him. What is permitted on the Sabbath inside the sanctuary is named specifically. Burning frankincense and bringing oblations and sacrifices before Yahuah (God) for days and for Sabbaths. This work alone shall be done on the Sabbath-days in the sanctuary of Yahuah your Elohim (the LORD your God); that they may atone for Yashar’el (Israel) with sacrifice continually from day to day for a memorial well-pleasing before Yahuah (God), and that He may receive them always from day to day according as you have been commanded. Verses 10–11. The priestly work in the sanctuary continues on the Sabbath. The body’s rest is structured around the priestly service; the priestly service does not violate the Sabbath because the priestly service is the body’s worship of the day’s Sovereign. The pattern is what Yahusha (Jesus) names in Matthew 12:5 — the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are blameless — and what Hebrews 4:9–10 names as the Sabbath rest that remains for the people of Elohim (God). The covenant body’s Sabbath is not the cessation of all activity; it is the suspension of the body’s own commerce in favor of the body’s worship of the Father. The pattern is consistent. Verse 13 closes the book. The man who does any of these things on the Sabbath shall die, so that the children of Yashar’el (Israel) shall observe the Sabbaths according to the commandments regarding the Sabbaths of the land, as it is written in the tables, which He gave into my hands that I should write out for you the laws of the seasons, and the seasons according to the division of their days. The book ends with the writing. The angel of the presence has written down what was on the heavenly tables; the writing is given into Moses’ hands; the writing is for the children of Yashar’el (Israel) to keep. The book that opened with the angel of the presence being commanded to write closes with the writing delivered. Herewith is completed the account of the division of the days. About the Author I was not raised in the Word. I was raised in the world—and like so many, I called myself a believer while never once opening the Book. I thought a good heart was enough. I thought moral living was righteousness. I thought believing in a name was the same as knowing the One who bore it. I was wrong—and YAHUAH (God) loved me too much to leave me that way. After baptism, with no root and no foundation, the adversary came—as he always does—and I fell. I didn’t just stumble. I ran. I ran from YAHUAH (God), into darkness, into failure, into everything the scripture warned against, and I burned in every direction I turned. The curses of Deuteronomy 28 became my life. My body broke down. Open wounds that would not heal. Sores that covered me. Pain that made it impossible to sit, stand, or sleep. I had become the man in the chapter—and I didn’t even know it yet. It was a chance encounter with an old friend that changed everything. He pointed me to the curses. I read. I wept. The Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) overwhelmed me—because I recognized myself on that page. You will flee when no one pursues. Wounds that will not heal. That was me. That had been me. And in that moment, I understood: YAHUAH (God) had not abandoned me. YAHUAH (God) had been pursuing me. I fell on my face and made one request: If it is not too late—take me back. I was baptized again. Demons were cast out. And then came the anointing—not a drop of oil on the forehead, but a full healing anointing poured over me, head to toe. When I finally wiped the oil from my eyes, the wounds were gone. Closed. Vanished. The eczema—gone. I wept and did not wash that oil off for weeks, because I knew what kind of miracle had just happened on my body. I kept my word. I dove into the scriptures with everything I had—barely sleeping, no job, fed by a friend, pouring over the Word every waking hour. After six months, the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) spoke and told me to shave my head. I researched for two weeks, asked for a second witness, received it, and shaved. My hair—black when I shaved it—grew back completely white. I was thirty years old, with a black beard and a white head, and I did not ask questions. I had learned who was boss. Years later, I prayed and asked YAHUAH (God) to give me a wife, bringing Him to remembrance of His Word—that it is not good for man to be alone. I began searching and finally found the woman He had chosen. The confirmation came to her through a dream. She had also been praying, asking YAHUAH (God) to reveal to her whom she was to marry—and she specifically asked that He tell her what I had so heavily on my heart to share before I ever told her. She asked that He speak audibly or through a dream so there would be no doubt. That night she did dream, and though she did not understand it at the time, it became clear to everyone once I had shared my testimony. She knew YAHUAH (God) had answered her. A week later I proposed. Within two months I had flown across the country to marry her, and after saying our vows I stuck out my hand and introduced myself. Other than a few photos, the first time we laid eyes on each other was when she walked down the aisle on our wedding day. That season did not last. I took time off from the Nazarite vow when family came. I started a business. I tried to build a life on my own terms. And like Jonah, I learned that YAHUAH (God) does not negotiate. The trouble that followed was of biblical proportions—perplexing, relentless, miraculous in its precision. It broke me down, literally, at a roadside where a stranger helped me. I thanked the man and prayed over him. The Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) spoke through me and blessed him. He looked up with tears and said, You will never know how badly I needed that. Then came the rebuke—sharp, clear, unmistakable: “I didn’t break you down here to help you, you rebel. I broke you down here to help him. I don’t care when you think your ministry is going to start. It starts today.” I took the Nazarite vow again—this time for life. That was a little over three years ago. I am a Nazarite for life, set apart to walk in every word that proceeds from the mouth of YAHUAH (God). No man has taught me that which I know. I follow no man, no teacher, no ministry—the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) alone has revealed these things to me, line upon line, precept upon precept, as YAHUAH (God) promised He would teach His own (Isaiah 28:9–10; John 16:13). I do not write to you as a scholar with degrees or a pastor with a pulpit. I write to you as a bondservant who was broken, healed, called, and sent—with nothing to offer except what the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) has shown me. And I will tell you this plainly: you will find the truth—the end declared from the beginning, that no one teaches. Not from the church. Not from the Hebrew roots community. Not from any ministry or movement you have sat under. If it sounds familiar in places, follow it further—because where it goes, most teachers have never dared to venture. I will tell you the truth about how this began. Like Jonah, I did not want to be a shepherd. I wanted to deliver the message and walk away—leave the truth on the page, let the reader take it or leave it, and keep my distance from the sheep. That was not humility. It was unwillingness in costume—the same posture as the outspoken Christian who shouts truth at strangers and never stays to feed them. The proclamation without the tending. Message without love. The Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) would not let me hide there. He has been shaving the calluses from my heart—circumcising it, as the Word promised in Deuteronomy 30:6—and what came up underneath was a love for the flock that does not let you turn back. I am called to be a shepherd under the Good Shepherd, Yahusha (Jesus), who was YAHUAH (God) in the flesh. The Chief Shepherd gathers the flock. The under-shepherd tends them, feeds them, stays with them, and lays down his life for them. I am still learning what that costs. I am still being polished. But the willingness is no longer in question. Everything in this work points back to the Word and to YAHUAH (God) alone—whether in the form He took to speak to Moses, or the flesh He took on to reveal Himself as Yahusha (Jesus). I am saved not by anything I have done but by grace through faith—the gift of Elohim (God), not of works, lest any man should boast (Ephesians 2:8–9). I keep His commandments because He saved me, not to be saved. I am not righteous. I am not good. I am only a man who tasted that YAHUAH (God) is good (Psalm 34:8) and has never recovered from it. Since then, I have walked set apart—ministering daily, engaging every person I come across, in person or online, giving freely everything YAHUAH (God) has shown me, holding nothing back. These books are the long form of that teaching, set in print so it can travel further than I can. I did not choose this. He chose it for me. And the only credential I carry is the one He burned into my life: I was dead, and He raised me. I was scattered, and He gathered me. I was a rebel, and He broke me until I wasn’t. If you have ever sensed that what you have been taught barely scratches the surface—you were right. That hunger was put there for a reason. These books were written for the one who is ready to follow the Word further than they have ever been taken. Test every spirit. Prove all things. Let the unchanging standard of His commandments be the judge (1 John 4:1; 1 Thessalonians 5:21). All glory belongs to YAHUAH (God). If there is truth here, it is His. If there is error, it is mine. Flee to the Word. Tremble at His Word. Return to all His commandments. And prepare—because the King is coming, and He is not coming to ask what we believed. He is coming to see what we did.
